definition_en: of a good enough standard; honest and kind
core_image: 一件洗得干净、不新却合身的衬衫
scene: 他穿着干净的旧衬衫去面试，看着让人放心。 He is a decent man who keeps his word.
sceneCN: 这里 decent 指「正派的」（第 3 个义项：为人端正）；句意他是个守信的正派人。

senses.title: Good enough in quality
senses.definition: acceptable in quality, though not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 质量可以接受，虽不算出色
senses.example: He finally found a decent job near home.
senses.exampleCN: 他终于在离家不远的地方找到一份像样的工作。
senses.why: A low bar is still a bar; decent marks the line above it.
senses.whyCN: 低的标准也是标准，decent 指的就是这条线以上。

senses.title: Proper and respectable
senses.definition: following accepted standards of dress or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 符合大家认可的穿着与举止标准
senses.example: Wear something decent to the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试时穿得体面一点。
senses.why: What is proper is decided by the eyes of other people.
senses.whyCN: 什么叫得体，是由别人的眼睛定的。

senses.title: Honest and kind
senses.definition: having good moral qualities
senses.definitionCN: 具备良好的品德
senses.example: He is a decent man who keeps his word.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个守信的正派人。
senses.why: The word turns from manners to morals without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从礼貌转到品行，外形一点没变。

intro.en: Decent came from Latin decens, fitting or becoming, from decere, to be proper.
intro.cn: decent 来自拉丁语 decens（合适的、相称的），源于 decere（应当、合宜）。

items.en: Decere meant to be fitting or proper for someone.
items.cn: decere 指对某人来说是合宜的。

items.en: Decens described what suits a person's place and duty.
items.cn: decens 形容与身份和职责相称的东西。

items.en: Décent carried the sense of proper and modest.
items.cn: décent 带着得体、有分寸的意思。

items.en: Decent named behaviour that met the standards of the day.
items.cn: decent 指符合当时标准的行为。

items.en: It softened into good enough, as in a decent meal.
items.cn: 后来它软化成「过得去」，比如一顿还不错的饭。

note.en: The look-alike group sounds close but means something else, and the meaning group runs from proper to merely acceptable.
note.cn: 形近组听着相近却另有意思，近义组则从得体走到勉强可以。

entries.definition: a movement downward
entries.definitionCN: 向下的移动

entries.definition: happening a short time ago
entries.definitionCN: 不久前发生的

entries.definition: to pour liquid into another container
entries.definitionCN: 把液体倒进另一个容器

entries.definition: considered proper by other people
entries.definitionCN: 被别人认为体面的

entries.definition: correct for the situation
entries.definitionCN: 合乎场合的

entries.definition: not too large or showy
entries.definitionCN: 不大也不张扬的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a clean old shirt and end with the quiet honesty behind it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一件干净的旧衬衫开始，落到衬衫背后的那份老实。

normal.en: A decent shirt is not new; it is clean and fits.
normal.cn: 体面的衬衫不必新，干净合身就行。

normal.en: Decent is the word for the middle, where most of life happens.
normal.cn: decent 是给中间地带用的词，而生活大多在那儿。

normal.en: Pay a decent wage and the work becomes decent too.
normal.cn: 给一份说得过去的工钱，活儿也跟着像样了。

normal.en: A decent man does the right thing when nobody is watching.
normal.cn: 正派的人，在没人看着时也做该做的事。

normal.en: One letter turns decent into descent, and the meaning falls away.
normal.cn: 换一个字母，decent 就成了 descent，意思一落千丈。

abstract.en: Picture a shirt ironed on a kitchen table.
abstract.cn: 想象一件在厨房桌上被熨平的衬衫。

abstract.en: Picture a meal that is plain, warm and enough.
abstract.cn: 想象一顿简单、热乎、吃得饱的饭。

abstract.en: Picture a man returning money he was never asked about.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把没人追问的钱还了回去。

examples.en: He is a decent man who keeps his word.
examples.cn: 他是个守信的正派人。

examples.en: She earns a decent salary and saves a little each month.
examples.cn: 她挣着一份不错的工资，每月还能存下一点。

examples.en: It was decent of you to wait for me.
examples.cn: 你等着我，真是厚道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decent 记成「得体身」：de 是得，cent 听起来像「身」，衣着得体、为人端正，就是得体身。

root: 来自拉丁语 decens（合宜的），源于 decere（应当如此），本义是「与身份相称」。经法语 décent 进入英语后先指合乎礼俗的举止，后来语气变软，日常里常表示「还过得去、像样」。

sensesIntro.en: From something acceptable, to something proper in others' eyes, to a person worth trusting.
sensesIntro.cn: 从还算可以的东西，到别人眼里得体的样子，再到值得信任的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clean, plain shirt that fits exactly.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件干净朴素、正好合身的衬衫。

branches.en: The first sense only asks that a thing be acceptable.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只要求东西过得去。

branches.en: The second sense adds the eyes of other people.
branches.cn: 第二个义项添上了旁人的目光。

branches.en: The third moves from appearance to the person behind it.
branches.cn: 第三个义项从外表走到了外表背后的那个人。

branches.en: Quality and propriety both rest on a shared minimum.
branches.cn: 质量和得体，都靠一条大家公认的底线。

branches.en: Good manners and good morals are neighbours in this word.
branches.cn: 在这个词里，礼貌与品德是邻居。

intro.en: Decent pairs with its negative and its noun: decency, indecent, indecency.
intro.cn: decent 与否定形式和名词配对：decency、indecent、indecency。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is decere, to be fitting; decus gave the related idea of honour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 decere（合宜），decus 则带来「荣誉、体面」的意思。

items.example: They live in a decent flat.
items.exampleCN: 他们住在一套还不错的公寓里。

items.example: He had the decency to apologise.
The sign was removed as indecent.
items.exampleCN: 那块招牌因不雅被拆掉了。

items.example: The court heard a charge of indecency.
items.exampleCN: 法庭审理了一项猥亵指控。

items.example: He was indecently dressed for the ceremony.
items.exampleCN: 他穿得不宜出席那个仪式。
他们找到一家看上去还像样的旅馆。

items.example: The flat has a decent-sized kitchen.
items.exampleCN: 这套公寓有个相当大的厨房。

latinEntries.example: Decere lies behind decent and decorum.
latinEntries.exampleCN: decere 是 decent 和 decorum 的来源。

definition_en: the state of taking part in something or of being connected with it, often as a matter of responsibility
core_image: 一只手伸进正在运转的机器里，成了它的一部分
scene: 社区中心墙上贴着排班表，好几位老人每周都来分菜。 Her involvement in the food bank began with one afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 involvement 是「参与」（第 1 个义项：主动投入某项活动），句意为她在食品银行的参与从某一个下午开始。画面里的物件：排班表、菜筐、记号笔。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ment 构成，义为「涉及；使卷入」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「参与的；复杂的」
同以 in- 开头、invol- 词干的形近词，义为「非自愿的」

senses.title: Taking an active part
senses.definition: the fact of actively giving your time or effort to an activity
senses.definitionCN: 主动把时间或精力投入到某项活动中的事实
senses.example: Her involvement in the choir gave her a way to make friends.
senses.exampleCN: 参加合唱团让她找到了交朋友的方式。
senses.why: The -ment noun turns the act of joining in into a lasting relation.
senses.whyCN: -ment 名词把「加入」这个动作变成一种持续的关系。

senses.title: Being connected to a trouble
senses.definition: the state of being linked to an accident, crime, or scandal
senses.definitionCN: 与事故、犯罪或丑闻被联系在一起的状态
senses.example: He denied any involvement in the theft.
senses.exampleCN: 他否认与这起盗窃有任何牵连。
senses.why: Here the wrapping is unwanted: a name rolled into a police file.
senses.whyCN: 这里的包裹是不情愿的：一个名字被卷进了警方的卷宗。

senses.title: Emotional commitment
senses.definition: a deep personal interest or feeling that makes leaving hard
senses.definitionCN: 一种让人难以抽身的深切私人兴趣或情感
senses.example: Her emotional involvement in the case tested her judgement.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这个案子的情感投入影响了她的判断。
senses.why: Feeling can be wrapped in too, and that is the heaviest kind of involvement.
senses.whyCN: 情感也会被卷进去，那是最沉的一种投入。

intro.en: Involvement is the noun from involve, which began as Latin involvere, "to wrap".
intro.cn: involvement 是 involve 的名词，而 involve 起初就是拉丁 involvere「包裹」。

items.en: volvere meant "to roll".
items.cn: volvere 意为「滚、卷」。

items.en: involvere meant "to roll in, to wrap".
items.cn: involvere 意为「卷进、包裹」。

items.en: French passed the verb in as involver.
items.cn: 法语以 involver 传入这个动词。

items.en: English added -ment to name the state of being wrapped in.
items.cn: 英语加 -ment 指「被包进去」的状态。

items.en: Modern usage splits the noun into participation and complicity.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个名词分成「参与」与「牵连」两面。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the involv- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for taking part.
note.cn: 形近组共用 involv- 词干；近义组收表示参与的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to include or entangle.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「涉及；卷入」，同族词。

entries.definition: Money put in for a return.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「投资」，开头相近。

entries.definition: Done without a choice.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「非自愿的」，同前缀。

entries.definition: The act of taking part in something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「参与」，最直接的对等词。

entries.definition: A promise and the effort to keep it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「投入；承诺」。

entries.definition: Involvement in wrongdoing with others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「同谋」，只用于坏事。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the noun back to a rolled-up sheet.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个名词系回一张卷好的纸。

normal.en: It is involve plus -ment, the state itself.
normal.cn: 它是 involve 加 -ment，指那个状态本身。

normal.en: You roll into an activity: that is involvement.
normal.cn: 你把自己卷进一项活动，这就是参与。

normal.en: You can roll into trouble just as easily.
normal.cn: 同样容易把自己卷进麻烦里。

normal.en: The -ment turns the act into a lasting condition.
normal.cn: -ment 把动作变成一种持续的状态。

normal.en: Denying involvement is a sentence you hear after scandals.
normal.cn: 丑闻之后总能听到「否认牵连」这句话。

abstract.en: Involvement is the footprint of an interest.
abstract.cn: 参与就是兴趣留下的脚印。

abstract.en: Being inside is warmth and also weight.
abstract.cn: 身在其中，既是温度也是重量。

abstract.en: Once wrapped in, you never unwrap completely.
abstract.cn: 一旦被卷进来，就很难完全卷出去。

examples.en: The school credits its success to parent involvement.
examples.cn: 学校把成功归功于家长的参与。

examples.en: The report found no involvement of local officials.
examples.cn: 报告认定没有当地官员牵涉其中。

examples.en: Her deep involvement with the study left little time for sleep.
examples.cn: 她对这个研究投入极深，几乎没时间睡觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: involve（卷入）+ ment（状态）——被卷进去的那种状态

root: 拉丁语 involvere「卷进去」→ involve → 加 -ment 成 involvement。同族有 involve、involved；形近 investment、involuntary。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: active part, connection to trouble, and emotional commitment.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：主动参与、与麻烦的牵连，以及感情上的投入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching into a running machine and staying there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸进运转的机器并留在里面。

branches.en: THE ROTA: hours written on a board and given away.
branches.cn: 排班表这条线：写在板上、交付出去的时间。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a name placed at a scene of trouble.
branches.cn: 记录这条线：名字被放到出事的地方。

branches.en: THE HEART: a case that will not let go of you.
branches.cn: 心这条线：一个放不下手的案子。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses are a tie between person and event.
branches.cn: 关联这条线：两个义项都是人与事件的连带。

branches.en: THE COST: what you give yourself to takes something back.
branches.cn: 代价这条线：你付出给的事也会取走些什么。

intro.en: Involvement is in- "into", volv- "roll", and -ment naming the state.
intro.cn: involvement 是 in-「进入」、volv-「卷」与标出状态的 -ment。

latinIntro.en: The family rests on Latin volvere and involvere, both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 这一族立足的拉丁语 volvere 与 involvere 均有记载。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的后盾。

items.example: The simplest member of the family.
A cousin that keeps the rolling image.

definition_zh: 加热器；暖气装置；炉子；热水器
definition_en: a device that is used to make something, especially a room or water, warmer
core_image: 一台把冷变热的机器：拧开开关，屋里渐渐暖起来
scene: 寒流来的那晚，水管冻住了，妈妈拧开旧机器的开关，过了一会儿热水又流了出来。 The old water heater finally started working again after a few minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 heater 是「热水器；加热装置」（第 3 个义项：给水加热的设备）；句意是那台旧热水器几分钟后终于又能正常工作了。

pos.zh: 加热器；暖气装置；热水器

collocations.zh: 空间取暖器；局部取暖器

derivatives.zh: 由动词 heat（加热）加名词后缀 -er 构成，义为「热；高温」
由动词 heat 加形容词后缀 -ed 构成，义为「加热过的；激烈的」
由动词 heat 加动名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「供暖；加热系统」
由前缀 re-（再）加动词 heat 构成，义为「重新加热」
由前缀 pre-（预先）加动词 heat 构成，义为「预热」

senses.title: A device that warms a room
senses.definition: a device that makes the air in a room or building warmer
senses.definitionCN: 让房间或建筑物里的空气变暖的装置
senses.example: She turned on the electric heater before getting out of bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她起床前先打开了电暖器。
senses.why: The suffix -er means a thing that does the action, so a heater is literally the thing that heats.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 表示「做某动作的东西」，heater 字面上就是「用来加热的东西」，最常见的就是给房间供暖的设备。

senses.title: The heating unit of a machine or vehicle
senses.titleCN: 机器或车内的暖气；加热部件
senses.definition: the part of a machine or vehicle that provides warm air
senses.definitionCN: 机器或车辆里提供暖空气的部件
senses.example: The heater in my car stopped working during the cold wave.
senses.exampleCN: 寒潮期间我车里的暖气坏了。
senses.why: Any machine that needs warmth carries a built-in unit that heats, and the -er suffix names that unit.
senses.whyCN: 任何需要热量的机器内部都装着一个负责加热的小部件，-er 后缀正好用来命名这个部件。

senses.title: A device that heats water
senses.definition: a device that warms water for washing or other uses
senses.definitionCN: 为洗漱或其他用途把水加热的设备
senses.example: Our water heater broke down, so we had to take cold showers.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的热水器坏了，只好洗冷水澡。
senses.why: The same naming rule applies to heating water: the device that heats is called a heater.
senses.whyCN: 同样的命名规则也适用于加热水：凡是负责加热的装置，一律用 heater 来称呼。

senses.title: A device for heating food or drink
senses.titleCN: 食物或饮品的加热器具
senses.definition: a small device used to warm food, drink, or baby bottles
senses.definitionCN: 用来加热食物、饮品或奶瓶的小型器具
senses.example: The campers used a portable heater to warm their soup.
senses.exampleCN: 露营的人用便携加热器热汤。
senses.why: Anything whose job is to heat, however small, earns the -er name of doer.
senses.whyCN: 只要职责是加热，哪怕体积很小，也同样按「加热者」的构词规则得名。

senses.title: An industrial heating unit
senses.titleCN: 工业加热炉；工业加热装置
senses.definition: a large piece of equipment that heats materials in factories or furnaces
senses.definitionCN: 工厂或熔炉里给物料加热的大型设备
senses.example: The steel plant replaced its old heater with a more efficient one.
senses.exampleCN: 钢厂用更高效的新加热炉换掉了旧设备。
senses.why: The naming rule scales up: large industrial machines that heat are still called heaters.
senses.whyCN: 命名规则可以放大：即使是给物料加热的大型工业机器，也沿用 heater 这个称呼。

senses.title: An engine starter aid in cold weather
senses.definition: a device that warms an engine before it starts in cold weather
senses.definitionCN: 寒冷天气下在启动前给发动机预热（或辅助预热）的装置
senses.example: Drivers in the north often plug in an engine heater on winter nights.
senses.exampleCN: 北方的司机冬夜里常给发动机预热器插电。
senses.why: Warming an engine before starting is still heating, so the device inherits the same name.
senses.whyCN: 启动前给发动机升温本质上仍是加热，所以这类装置顺理成章继承了同一个名字。

senses.title: A component that keeps a temperature steady
senses.definition: a component inside an appliance that keeps something at a set temperature
senses.definitionCN: 电器内部把某物维持在设定温度的元件
senses.example: The aquarium heater keeps the water at a constant temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼缸加热棒让水温保持恒定。
senses.why: Keeping warm is the same job as heating, so the word covers steady-temperature devices too.
senses.whyCN: 「保温」与「加热」本是同一件事的两面，所以这个词也覆盖维持恒温的元件。

senses.title: Figurative: a source of warmth or comfort
senses.titleCN: 比喻：带来温暖的人或事物
senses.definition: a person or thing that gives emotional warmth, used playfully
senses.definitionCN: 口语戏称给人带来温暖和安全感的人或事物
senses.example: Her hugs were the best heater in the freezing classroom.
senses.exampleCN: 在冰冷的教室里，她的拥抱就是最棒的暖炉。
senses.why: Because the core image is producing warmth, people borrow the word to describe emotional warmth.
senses.whyCN: 因为核心意象是「制造温暖」，人们顺势借用这个词来戏称带来情感温暖的人或物。

intro.en: Heater is a transparent English formation: the verb heat plus the agent suffix -er, first recorded as a device name in the early nineteenth century.
intro.cn: heater 是一个构词一目了然的英语词：动词 heat 加表「施动者／工具」的后缀 -er，作为设备名称首见于十九世纪初。

items.en: The verb heat goes back to the reconstructed Proto-Germanic form *haitjan, meaning to make hot, built on the root *hait- hot.
items.cn: 动词 heat 可追溯到重构的原始日耳曼语形式 *haitjan，义为「使变热」，建立在表「热」的词根 *hait- 之上。

items.en: Old English had hat, meaning hot, and hatian, meaning to become hot; the causative idea of making something hot developed alongside it.
items.cn: 古英语中有 hat（热的）和 hatian（变热），「使某物变热」的使动含义随之发展。

items.en: In Middle English the verb appeared as heten, and the form heat gradually settled into standard use by the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语时期动词写作 heten，到十六世纪 heat 这一形式逐渐定型为标准用法。

items.en: The suffix -er, from Old English -ere, marks a person or thing that performs an action, making heater mean the thing that heats.
items.cn: 后缀 -er 来自古英语 -ere，标记执行动作的人或物，于是 heater 的字面义就是「用来加热的东西」。

items.en: As an everyday device name, heater became common in the early nineteenth century with the spread of stoves, boilers, and domestic warming equipment.
items.cn: 作为日常设备名，heater 在十九世纪初随着炉具、锅炉和家用取暖设备的普及而变得常见。

items.en: Today heater covers everything from car heaters and water heaters to space heaters, wherever the job is producing warmth.
items.cn: 如今从车载暖气、热水器到空间取暖器，凡以产生热量为职责的设备，都可以叫 heater。

note.en: Heater belongs to the small heat word family; be careful to tell it apart from look-alike words that merely share a spelling shape.
note.cn: heater 属于小小的「热」词族；注意把它与只是拼写形状相似的词区分开。

entries.definition: the quality of being hot, or the act of making something hot
entries.definitionCN: 热；高温；加热（heater 的基础动词与名词）

entries.definition: the system or process of keeping a building warm
entries.definitionCN: 供暖；供暖系统（由 heat 加 -ing 构成）

entries.definition: having no heater; rare descriptive form
entries.definitionCN: 无加热装置的（少见描述性形式，由 heater 加 -less 构成）

entries.definition: the floor of a fireplace; the area in front of it
entries.definitionCN: 壁炉地面；炉边——只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同，勿混淆

entries.definition: loud, cheerful, and full of energy
entries.definitionCN: 热情的； hearty 与 heart 同源，与 heater 只是拼写相近，词源无关

entries.definition: a device that burns fuel or uses electricity for cooking or warming a room
entries.definitionCN: 炉子；炉灶（侧重烹饪，也可取暖）

entries.definition: an enclosed chamber for very high heat, in industry or home heating
entries.definitionCN: 熔炉；暖气锅炉（规模更大、温度更高）

entries.definition: a device that gives out heat from hot water or steam inside it
entries.definitionCN: 暖气片；散热器（以辐射方式散热的供暖设备）

entries.definition: a tank or device that heats water, especially for a heating system
entries.definitionCN: 锅炉；热水器（侧重加热水供供暖使用）

entries.definition: a small device or container that keeps something warm
entries.definitionCN: 保温器；保温容器（侧重保温而非强力加热）

normalIntro.en: Build the word from its two visible parts and connect each memory to a real device you have used.
normalIntro.cn: 把这个词拆成两个看得见的部分来记，并把每条联想连到你真实用过的设备上。

normal.en: heat + er = the thing that heats; the -er suffix names the doer or tool.
normal.cn: heat（加热）+ -er（做……的东西）＝加热器；-er 是「执行者」后缀。

normal.en: Same pattern as cooker, cooler, and dryer: appliance names love the -er suffix.
normal.cn: 与 cooker（炊具）、cooler（冰箱）、dryer（烘干机）同一构词法：家电名偏爱 -er 后缀。

normal.en: water heater, space heater, car heater: the compound tells you what it heats.
normal.cn: water heater（热水器）、space heater（取暖器）、car heater（车载暖气）：复合词告诉你它加热什么。

normal.en: Winter scene memory: when the room is cold, you turn on the heater, so heater belongs to cold days.
normal.cn: 冬景记忆法：屋里一冷就打开 heater，让这个词和寒冷的冬天绑定在一起。

normal.en: Compare with heat itself: heat is the warmth, heater is the machine that makes the warmth.
normal.cn: 与 heat 对比记忆：heat 是热本身，heater 是制造热的机器。

abstract.en: Picture a little machine with arms, hugging cold air and pushing it out warm.
abstract.cn: 想象一台长着手臂的小机器，抱住冷空气，再把暖风推出来。

abstract.en: See a red switch glowing on a snowy night; the switch is the heater waking up.
abstract.cn: 雪夜里一个发红光的开关亮起，那是 heater 正在苏醒。

abstract.en: Think of -er as a tiny worker label: heater is the worker whose only job is heat.
abstract.cn: 把 -er 想成小工人标签：heater 就是唯一职责是「加热」的那名工人。

examples.en: Please turn off the heater before you leave the office.
examples.cn: 离开办公室前请关掉取暖器。

examples.en: The water heater in our flat broke down again this winter.
examples.cn: 今年冬天我们公寓的热水器又坏了。

examples.en: A gentle rain fell all afternoon and the wind grew cold.
examples.cn: 细雨下了一下午，风越来越冷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑特儿」——屋子里黑黑的特别冷，赶紧打开「黑特儿」（加热器）取暖；谐音仅助记，heater 实际由 heat 加 -er 构成。

root: heater 是地道的英语本土构词：词根为古英语 hat（热的）与动词 hatian（变热），中英语发展为 heten，现代英语定型为动词 heat（加热）；后缀 -er 来自古英语 -ere，表「做某事的人或物」。heat + -er ＝「用来加热的装置」。无拉丁或希腊词根，构词完全透明。

sensesIntro.en: From the core image of a device that produces warmth, heater spreads to room heaters, car heaters, water heaters, small warming tools, industrial units, engine pre-warmers, steady-temperature parts, and playful figurative uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「制造温暖的装置」这一核心意象出发，heater 依次覆盖房间取暖器、车载暖气、热水器、小型加热器具、工业加热炉、发动机预热器、恒温元件，以及戏称带来温暖的比喻用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a device whose only job is to make something warmer
core.cn: 核心意象：一台唯一职责是把东西变暖的装置

branches.en: Room and space warming devices, the most common everyday use
branches.cn: 房间与空间取暖设备，最常见的日常用法

branches.en: Heating units inside machines and vehicles, including engine pre-warmers
branches.cn: 机器与车辆内部的加热部件，包括发动机预热器

branches.en: Devices that heat water, food, drink, or baby bottles
branches.cn: 加热水、食物、饮品或奶瓶的器具

branches.en: Large industrial heating units and steady-temperature components
branches.cn: 大型工业加热炉与维持恒温的元件

branches.en: Playful figurative use for a person or thing that gives emotional warmth
branches.cn: 戏称带来情感温暖的人或物的比喻用法

intro.en: Heater is built from a native English verb plus one productive suffix; the same pattern names dozens of household appliances.
intro.cn: heater 由一个英语本土动词加一个高产后缀构成；同样的模式命名了几十种家用电器。

latinIntro.en: Heater has no Latin root of its own, but the -er agent idea and the heat concept connect it to Latin-derived relatives worth knowing.
latinIntro.cn: heater 本身没有拉丁词根，但「-er 施动者」的思路和「热」的概念能把它与拉丁来源的相关词联系起来。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does an action

items.meaning: the act or system of doing something

items.meaningCN: 热（希腊来源，与 heat 概念相对）

items.meaning: a thing that does an action, Latin counterpart of -er
items.meaningCN: 做某动作之物（-er 的拉丁对应形式）

latinEntries.exampleCN: 熔炉；锅炉——经由古法语传入英语

definition_zh: 平均数；平均的；普通的；平均为
definition_en: the middle amount or level, or to amount to such a level
core_image: 一排高低不齐的柱子被一条水平线穿过
scene: 老师在讲台上翻开成绩册。 The average score of the class rose this term.
sceneCN: 这里 average 是「平均数」（第 1 个义项：把总数按份数均分得到的值）；句意是这个班的平均分本学期提高了。

derivatives.zh: 由 average 加 -ly 构成，义为「平均地；普通地」
由 average 与 sized 复合而成，义为「中等大小的」

senses.title: The middle amount
senses.definition: the result of adding several amounts and dividing by their number
senses.definitionCN: 把若干数量相加后除以个数所得的结果
senses.example: The average of three, five and seven is five.
senses.exampleCN: 三、五、七的平均数是五。
senses.why: Average comes from French avarie, damage to goods at sea, because a shared loss was divided among merchants; the arithmetic sense grew from dividing a total fairly.
senses.whyCN: average 来自法语 avarie「海损」，因为共同损失要由商人分摊；算术上的「平均」正是从这种平摊长出来的。

senses.title: Typical or ordinary
senses.definition: ordinary and not special or unusual
senses.definitionCN: 普通而并无特别之处的
senses.example: She is an average student who works hard.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个努力用功的普通学生。
senses.why: If an average is the middle of a range, then a person or thing near that middle is ordinary, neither very good nor very bad.
senses.whyCN: 既然平均数是区间的中点，那么处在中点附近的人或物就是普通的，不算特别好也不算特别差。

senses.title: To amount to as a mean
senses.definition: to reach an average of a particular amount over time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间里达到某个平均数值
senses.example: Sales averaged two hundred units a month.
senses.exampleCN: 每月销量平均为两百件。
senses.why: The noun meaning the middle value turned into a verb meaning to produce that middle value over time.
senses.whyCN: 表示中间值的名词转成动词，就表示在一段时间里得出那个平均值。

intro.en: Average began as a word about shared loss at sea.
intro.cn: average 最初是一个讲海上共同损失的说法。

items.en: habere meant 'to have', the base of later French forms.
items.cn: habere 意为「有」，是后来法语词形的词基。

items.en: awariya meant damaged goods.
items.cn: awariya 意为受损的货物。

items.en: avarie meant damage to a ship or its cargo.
items.cn: avarie 意为船只或货物的损失。

items.en: averay meant a charge shared by merchants.
items.cn: averay 意为商人分摊的费用。

items.en: The word settled on the sense of a middle value.
items.cn: 这个词最后固定为「平均值」之义。

note.en: The look-alike group starts with a short a; the near-meaning group gives middle and ordinary words.
note.cn: 形近组都以短促的 a 起头；近义组是表示中间与普通的词。

entries.definition: to state something firmly
entries.definitionCN: 断言

entries.definition: to punish someone for a wrong
entries.definitionCN: 为……报仇

entries.definition: to turn away or prevent
entries.definitionCN: 转移；避免

entries.definition: the middle value of a set of numbers
entries.definitionCN: 平均值

entries.definition: showing the usual qualities
entries.definitionCN: 典型的

entries.definition: not special in any way
entries.definitionCN: 普通的

normalIntro.en: Average turns uneven amounts into one flat level and then calls that level ordinary.
normalIntro.cn: average 把高低不齐的数量摊成一条水平线，再把这个水平称作普通。

normal.en: Average has three syllables, with the stress on the first.
normal.cn: average 有三个音节，重音在第一个。

normal.en: Use on average to speak about a general level.
normal.cn: 谈总体水平时用 on average。

normal.en: As a verb, average takes no preposition.
normal.cn: 作动词时 average 不加介词。

normal.en: Above average and below average mark the two sides.
normal.cn: 高于平均与低于平均分别标出两侧。

normal.en: Do not confuse average with avarice, which means greed.
normal.cn: 别把 average 与表示贪婪的 avarice 混淆。

abstract.en: See a row of uneven bars with one flat line through them.
abstract.cn: 想象一排高低不齐的柱子被一条水平线穿过。

abstract.en: See several cups of water poured into one wide jar.
abstract.cn: 想象几杯水倒进一只宽口罐里。

abstract.en: See a crowd where most heads reach the same height.
abstract.cn: 想象人群里大多数脑袋都一样高。

examples.en: The average score of the class rose this term.
examples.cn: 这个班的平均分本学期提高了。

examples.en: On average, the train arrives ten minutes late.
examples.cn: 平均而言，这趟火车晚点十分钟。

examples.en: Sales averaged two hundred units a month.
examples.cn: 每月销量平均为两百件。

dict_mnemonic.text: a- 加 ver 加 -age：把高低不齐的数摊平到同一条线上，就是平均数，也就是普普通通的水平。

root: 源自法语 avarie「海损」，上溯至意大利语 avaria，可能来自阿拉伯语 awariya「受损货物」；由商人平摊损失引申为「平均分担」，再固定为「平均数」。

sensesIntro.en: A fair share, a middle value and an ordinary level are one idea seen from three sides.
sensesIntro.cn: 平摊、中间值与普通水平，是同一个想法的三个侧面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat line cutting through uneven heights.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条水平线穿过高低不齐的柱子。

branches.en: the average of the scores
branches.cn: 分数的平均数

branches.en: on average
branches.cn: 平均而言

branches.en: an average student
branches.cn: 普通学生

branches.en: average height
branches.cn: 中等身高

branches.en: sales averaged ten
branches.cn: 销量平均为十

intro.en: The ending -age is a French noun marker, and average still behaves like a French borrowing.
intro.cn: 词尾 -age 是法语名词标记，average 至今仍像法语借词。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere, 'to have', lies behind several French forms that shaped average.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habere「有」藏在几个塑造 average 的法语词形之后。
