definition_zh: 无论如何；不管怎样；随便地；草率地；杂乱地
definition_en: in any way; also in spite of that, or in a careless and untidy manner
core_image: 路怎么走都行，反正要到那个地方去
scene: 山间岔路口，两个旅人看了看被雨冲坏的路牌。 Anyhow, we can still reach the village before dark.
sceneCN: 这里 anyhow 是「无论如何」（第 1 个义项：不管用什么方式、有什么阻碍，结论照旧成立）；句意为「无论如何，我们还是能在天黑前赶到村里」。画面里有山间岔路口、被雨冲坏的路牌和两个停下来商量的旅人。

pos.zh: 副词：无论如何；不管怎样；随便地；草率地

collocations.zh: 横七竖八地；勉强凑合地

derivatives.zh: 由 anyway 类推加 -s 形成的口语变体，义为「反正、无论如何」
由 any 加后缀 -wise 构成，义为「以任何方式」，现为古旧用法
由 any 与 way 构成的同族复合词，义为「无论如何、反正」

senses.title: In spite of everything
senses.definition: used to say that something remains true or will still happen despite what has just been said
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示尽管刚说过某种情况，某事仍然成立或仍会发生
senses.example: We missed the last bus, but anyhow we walked home.
senses.exampleCN: 我们错过了末班车，不过反正还是走回了家。
senses.why: The word began as 'any way at all'; once every route is allowed, obstacles stop being decisive, and the conclusion holds regardless.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是「随便哪种方式都行」；当每条路都被允许，阻碍就不再起决定作用，结论也就照旧成立。

senses.title: In any manner whatsoever
senses.definition: in any way or by any method, with the method left entirely open
senses.definitionCN: 以任何方式或任何方法，方法本身完全敞开
senses.example: Try to open the jar anyhow you can; the lid is stuck.
senses.exampleCN: 盖子是卡住的，你想用什么办法打开这个罐子都行。
senses.why: Here the compound is still literal: any plus how, every possible method laid on the table at once.
senses.whyCN: 这里复合词仍取字面义：any 加 how，所有可能的办法一次性摊在桌上。

senses.title: Carelessly, without method
senses.definition: done without care, order, or proper method
senses.definitionCN: 做事不讲心思、顺序或正当方法
senses.example: He does his work anyhow and never checks the figures.
senses.exampleCN: 他做事随随便便，从不核对数字。
senses.why: If any way will do, then no way is chosen carefully; the open choice curdles into carelessness.
senses.whyCN: 如果哪种方式都行，那就没有一种被认真挑选；敞开的选择由此凝结成草率。

senses.title: Untidily, in disorder
senses.definition: placed or arranged without order, so that things lie in a jumble
senses.definitionCN: 摆放或安排没有次序，东西堆成一团乱
senses.example: The shelves were stacked anyhow, with cans behind boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 架子上的东西堆得横七竖八，罐头都塞在箱子后面。
senses.why: The physical picture grows out of the careless sense: when placement follows no plan, the result looks like a heap.
senses.whyCN: 这个具体的画面从「草率」一义长出来：摆放不依任何计划，结果就成了一堆。

senses.title: Anyway, to close a topic
senses.definition: used in speech to end a topic or return to the main point, much like anyway
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用于结束一个话题或回到正题，作用近似 anyway
senses.example: Anyhow, that is the story; now let us get back to work.
senses.exampleCN: 总之，故事就是这样；现在我们回去干活吧。
senses.why: A word that dismisses obstacles is ready-made for dismissing side topics, so it becomes a conversational hinge.
senses.whyCN: 一个能打发障碍的词，天生也适合打发枝节话题，于是它成了会话里的转轴。

intro.en: Anyhow is a native compound of any and how, built in English rather than borrowed from another language.
intro.cn: anyhow 是 any 与 how 构成的本族复合词，是在英语内部造出来的，并非从别的语言借入。

items.en: The interrogative hū 'how' is old and common, and ǣnig 'any' already existed beside it.
items.cn: 疑问词 hū「如何」古老而常用，ǣnig「任何一个」当时也已与它并存。

items.en: The two words are joined as any how, first meaning 'in any manner', literally any possible way of doing something.
items.cn: 两个词合成 any how，最初表示「以任何方式」，字面就是做某事的任何一种可能办法。

items.en: The spelling closes into anyhow, and the word begins to carry the concessive sense 'in spite of that'.
items.cn: 拼写合拢为 anyhow，这个词开始带上让步义「尽管如此」。

items.en: The careless sense 'in a slovenly way' becomes common in descriptions of work and arrangement.
items.cn: 「草率、马虎」这一义项在描写干活与摆放的文字里变得常见。

items.en: In speech anyhow also serves as a topic closer, a role it shares with anyway; the literal 'any way' sense survives chiefly in set phrases.
items.cn: 口语中 anyhow 还充当收束话题的词，这一角色与 anyway 共有；字面的「任何方式」义主要活在固定短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the close compounds and variants; the near-meaning group gathers the connectives and adverbs that express the same concession.
note.cn: 形近组收与它最接近的复合词和变体；近义组收表达同样让步关系的连接词与副词。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in spite of that, the closest twin of anyhow.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「无论如何、反正」，是 anyhow 最接近的对应词。

entries.definition: A colloquial variant of anyway, common in informal speech.
entries.definitionCN: anyway 的口语变体，常见于非正式谈话。

entries.definition: An archaic adverb meaning in any manner.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧副词，义为「以任何方式」。

entries.definition: A connective meaning despite that, used to contrast two statements.
entries.definitionCN: 连接词，义为「然而、尽管如此」，用于对比前后两句，语气比 anyhow 正式。

entries.definition: A formal connective meaning in spite of that.
entries.definitionCN: 正式连接词，义为「尽管如此」，书面语气最强。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning without being affected by the circumstances.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「不加理会、无论如何」，强调不受情况影响。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in a random, unplanned way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「随意地、杂乱地」，与 anyhow 的草率义最接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real any-plus-how structure and the different sentence positions the word occupies.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 any 加 how 结构，以及这个词占据的不同句子位置。

normal.en: Split it: any plus how. Every possible method is left on the table.
normal.cn: 拆开看：any 加 how，每一种可能的办法都被摊在桌上。

normal.en: At the start of a sentence it concedes: anyhow, we can still get there.
normal.cn: 放在句首时它在让步：无论如何，我们还是能到那儿。

normal.en: Its twin is anyway; both began as 'any way at all'.
normal.cn: 它的孪生兄弟是 anyway，两者都由「随便哪条路都行」开始。

normal.en: If any way will do, no way is chosen: that is how it comes to mean carelessly.
normal.cn: 如果哪条路都行，就没有哪条被选中，这就是它转而表示草率的原因。

normal.en: Use it to close a topic, the way a hand waves a side issue away.
normal.cn: 用它收束话题，就像用手把枝节问题一挥而去。

abstract.en: Picture a road sign with every arrow pointing, and a walker who shrugs and takes any of them.
abstract.cn: 想象一块路牌上所有箭头都指着方向，而走路的人耸耸肩，随便挑了其中一个。

abstract.en: The word is a shrug turned into sound: obstacles are admitted, then brushed aside.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一声耸肩变成了声音：承认阻碍存在，然后把它拂开。

abstract.en: Carelessness is the shadow side: a choice so open that no choice is made.
abstract.cn: 草率是它的暗面：选择太敞开，以至于等于没有选择。

examples.en: We missed the last bus, but anyhow we walked home.
examples.cn: 我们错过了末班车，不过反正还是走回了家。

examples.en: The shelves were stacked anyhow, with cans behind boxes.
examples.cn: 架子上的东西堆得横七竖八，罐头都塞在箱子后面。

examples.en: Anyhow, that is the story; now let us get back to work.
examples.cn: 总之，故事就是这样；现在我们回去干活吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安妮好」——路都被雨冲坏了，旅人还是说「安妮好，能到」：无论如何

root: anyhow 由 any「任何一个」与 how「如何」在本族英语中复合而成。十六世纪写作 any how，义为「以任何方式」；十七世纪拼写合拢，并发展出让步义「尽管如此」；十九世纪又生出「草率、杂乱」的具体义；现代口语里还兼任收束话题的转轴，作用与 anyway 相近。

sensesIntro.en: Five uses fan out from 'any way at all': the concessive 'in spite of that', the literal open method, the careless manner, the untidy result, and the conversational topic closer.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个用法从「随便哪条路都行」展开：让步的「尽管如此」、字面的开放方法、草率的方式、杂乱的结果，以及会话中收束话题的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every route is allowed, so no obstacle can decide the outcome.
core.cn: 核心意象：每条路都被允许，于是任何阻碍都无法决定结果。

branches.en: THE CONCESSION LINE: obstacles are admitted, yet the conclusion stands.
branches.cn: 让步线：承认阻碍存在，结论却照旧立住。

branches.en: THE METHOD LINE: every possible way of doing it is left open.
branches.cn: 方法线：每一种可行的做法都敞开着。

branches.en: THE CARELESS LINE: when any way will do, none is chosen with care.
branches.cn: 草率线：既然哪条路都行，就没有一条被认真挑选。

branches.en: THE DISORDER LINE: placement without a plan turns into a heap.
branches.cn: 杂乱线：不依计划的摆放堆成一团。

branches.en: THE HINGE LINE: the same shrug waves a side topic away.
branches.cn: 转轴线：同一次耸肩把枝节话题也挥走了。

intro.en: Anyhow is transparently built: any plus how, with parallel compounds on way, wise and thing.
intro.cn: anyhow 的构造一目了然：any 加 how，并有 way、wise、thing 等平行复合形式。

latinIntro.en: Anyhow has no Latin source. Latin interrogative words such as qualis are parallels in function only.
latinIntro.cn: anyhow 没有拉丁语来源。像 qualis 这样的拉丁语疑问词只是在功能上平行。

items.meaning: in any way; in spite of that
items.example: Anyhow, the door was already open.
How did you find the hidden path?
items.exampleCN: 你是怎么找到那条隐蔽小路的？

items.example: Anyway, the train has not left yet.

items.meaningCN: 口语中的「反正、无论如何」

items.example: The old tools were not anywise useful.
items.exampleCN: 那些旧工具怎么都用不上。

items.meaning: in some way not yet known
items.meaningCN: 以某种尚不清楚的方式
items.example: Somehow the letter arrived on time.
items.exampleCN: 那封信不知怎么就按时到了。

items.example: However you arrange it, the frame stays level.
items.exampleCN: 无论你怎么摆，这个框架都保持水平。

items.meaningCN: 在复合副词中表示「方式」的构词成分
items.example: It marks the manner inside the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它在复合词内部标记方式。

items.meaning: one or some, no matter which
items.example: Any of the three roads will do.

definition_zh: 肌肉；肌力；体力；影响力；实力
definition_en: body tissue made of fibres that can contract and produce movement, or the strength and power that such tissue gives
core_image: 一束束能自己收紧的绳索，一收紧就把相连的骨头拉动
scene: 健身房教练让学员把手贴上上臂，感受发力时那团组织的变化： He felt the muscle tighten under his hand.
sceneCN: 这里指「一块肌肉」（第 2 个义项：作为解剖单位的一块肌肉）；句意为他把手按在上臂，感到那块肌肉绷紧；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 力量；体力；（政治、军事上的）实力

forms.label: 形容词（肌肉的；肌肉发达的）
动词（强行挤入；使劲搬动）

derivatives.zh: 肌肉的；肌肉发达的；强有力的

senses.title: Contractile tissue
senses.titleCN: 肌肉组织：能收缩的纤维组织
senses.definition: tissue built from fibres that shorten when stimulated and so produce movement
senses.definitionCN: 由受刺激会缩短的纤维构成、从而产生运动的组织
senses.example: Skeletal muscle is built from long fibres that shorten when a nerve signal arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 骨骼肌由长纤维构成，神经信号到达时这些纤维会缩短。
senses.why: The core of the word is not shape but action: the tissue exists to pull, and only contraction makes it useful.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心不是形状而是动作：这种组织为拉动而生，只有收缩才使它有用。

senses.title: A single muscle organ
senses.titleCN: 一块肌肉：解剖学上的独立单位
senses.definition: one named bundle of muscle tissue with its own attachments, such as the biceps
senses.definitionCN: 一束有名称、有自身附着点的肌肉组织，如肱二头肌
senses.example: The surgeon repaired the muscle that controls the shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生修复了控制肩部的那块肌肉。
senses.why: Anatomy counts bundles rather than the material, so the mass of tissue becomes a countable organ with a name.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学按束计数而不按材料计数，于是整团组织变成有名字、可计数的器官。

senses.title: Smooth muscle
senses.titleCN: 平滑肌：内脏壁上的不随意肌
senses.definition: the involuntary muscle found in the walls of blood vessels and internal organs
senses.definitionCN: 分布于血管壁与内脏壁、不受意志控制的肌肉
senses.example: Smooth muscle in the artery wall narrows the vessel and raises blood pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 动脉壁的平滑肌使血管变窄，从而升高血压。
senses.why: The same contractile tissue works without orders from the will, so it is classified by where it sits and how it is controlled.
senses.whyCN: 同一种收缩组织可以不听意志指挥，因此按所在位置与控制方式另行分类。

senses.title: Cardiac muscle
senses.titleCN: 心肌：持续搏动的特化肌肉
senses.definition: the muscle of the heart wall, which contracts rhythmically without resting
senses.definitionCN: 心壁的肌肉，有节律地收缩且从不休息
senses.example: Cardiac muscle keeps beating without rest for a lifetime.
senses.exampleCN: 心肌一生都在跳动，从不休息。
senses.why: Heart muscle is a special case: it is striated like skeletal muscle but works continuously and involuntarily.
senses.whyCN: 心肌是个特例：它像骨骼肌一样有横纹，却持续工作且不受意志控制。

senses.title: Physical strength
senses.definition: the strength of the body, thought of as the power its muscles supply
senses.definitionCN: 身体的力量，被看作肌肉提供的力量
senses.example: It took real muscle to move the piano up the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 把钢琴搬上楼确实费了不少力气。
senses.why: Strength is what muscle does, so the tissue name is used for the force itself, much as brains can stand for intelligence.
senses.whyCN: 力量是肌肉做的事，于是组织名称被用来指这种力，就像「头脑」一词可以指智力一样。

senses.title: Influence and pressure
senses.definition: power to make things happen, especially when used to push a plan through
senses.definitionCN: 推动事情办成的力量，尤指用来推动某项计划
senses.example: The mayor put muscle behind the housing plan and forced a vote.
senses.exampleCN: 市长为住房计划施加影响，推动了表决。
senses.why: Political force is imagined as bodily force: you lean on people the way a muscle leans on a load.
senses.whyCN: 政治力量被想象成身体力量：你对人施压，正如肌肉对重物施力。

senses.title: Military or economic power
senses.titleCN: 军事或经济实力（展示实力）
senses.definition: visible national or corporate power, displayed to discourage rivals
senses.definitionCN: 为震慑对手而展示的国家或企业实力
senses.example: The country showed its military muscle in a large joint exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家通过大规模联合演习展示军事实力。
senses.why: The display is the point: the tissue is shown rather than used, and the show is meant to be seen and feared.
senses.whyCN: 展示本身就是目的：实力被亮出来而不一定真正使用，亮的目的是让人看见并忌惮。

senses.title: Muscle memory
senses.titleCN: 肌肉记忆：熟练到无需思考的动作
senses.definition: movement skills stored so deeply by practice that they feel automatic
senses.definitionCN: 经反复练习深植、几乎自动完成的动作技能
senses.example: After years of practice, the moves are stored in muscle memory.
senses.exampleCN: 多年练习之后，这些动作已存入肌肉记忆。
senses.why: The body seems to remember what the mind no longer rehearses, so the tissue is credited with the memory.
senses.whyCN: 身体似乎记住了头脑不再预演的东西，于是这份记忆被归到肌肉名下。

intro.en: Muscle goes back to Latin musculus, literally little mouse, a diminutive of mus mouse. The image is usually explained as a moving bulge under the skin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: muscle 可追溯到拉丁语 musculus，字面义「小老鼠」，是 mus「老鼠」的指小形式。一般认为这个形象来自皮下随动作鼓动的一块。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin musculus meant both a little mouse and a muscle. Roman writers already used it for the fleshy moving parts of the body.
items.cn: 拉丁 musculus 既指「小老鼠」，也指「肌肉」。罗马作家已用它指身体中会鼓动的肉。

items.en: The common explanation is that a muscle moving under the skin looked like a mouse running beneath cloth. This is generally accepted as an image, but it is a popular explanation rather than a documented ancient statement.
items.cn: 通常的解释是：皮下活动的肌肉像一只在布下跑动的老鼠。这一形象一般被认为是来源，但它属于通行解释，并非有明文记载的古人说明。

items.en: Greek mys meant both mouse and muscle, showing that the double meaning is very old and not a Latin invention.
items.cn: 希腊语 mys 同时指老鼠与肌肉，说明这种双重含义非常古老，并非拉丁语的独创。

items.en: The ancestor is reconstructed as PIE mus-, seen in several branches of the family; the form is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 其祖词被重构为原始印欧语 mus-，见于语系的多个分支；这一形式是重构形式，并非有书证的词。

items.en: Old French muscle carried the anatomical sense into English in the fourteenth century. The spelling kept the Latin -culus stem but dropped the ending.
items.cn: 古法语 muscle 在 14 世纪把解剖义带入英语。拼写保留了拉丁词干 -culus，但去掉了词尾。

items.en: The division into skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle belongs to seventeenth- to nineteenth-century physiology; the exact dates of each label are uncertain.
items.cn: 把肌肉分为骨骼肌、平滑肌与心肌，属于 17 至 19 世纪的生理学工作；各名称的准确年代已难确考。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound like muscle; the second holds body parts and strength words that are often used in its place.
note.cn: 第一组是与 muscle 形近或音近的词；第二组是常被用来替代它的身体部位词与力量词。

entries.definition: A sea shellfish with a dark shell. It sounds exactly like muscle but has no anatomical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 一种深色贝壳的海产贝类。读音与 muscle 完全相同，但没有解剖义。

entries.definition: The snout of an animal, or a device fitted over it; the ending is -le after a z sound, not -cle.
entries.definitionCN: 动物的口鼻部，或套在其上的装置；结尾是 z 音后的 -le，而不是 -cle。

entries.definition: The adjective of muscle, meaning relating to muscle or well developed; it cannot replace the noun.
entries.definitionCN: muscle 的形容词，意为「肌肉的」或「肌肉发达的」，不能替代名词。

entries.definition: The whole system of muscles in a body or a region, not one single muscle.
entries.definitionCN: 一个身体或一个部位的全部肌肉系统，而非单独一块肌肉。

entries.definition: A strong cord that attaches muscle to bone; it carries the pull but cannot contract itself.
entries.definitionCN: 把肌肉连到骨的强韧索带；它传递拉力，但自身不能收缩。

entries.definition: A band that holds bone to bone and stabilises a joint; it does not generate movement.
entries.definitionCN: 把骨与骨系住、稳定关节的带状结构；它不产生运动。

entries.definition: An older English word for a tendon, and figuratively for strength; muscle is the flesh that pulls it.
entries.definitionCN: 指肌腱的古老英语词，也可比喻力量；肌肉则是拉动它的那团肉。

entries.definition: Muscular strength, especially of a heavy build; it names the power rather than the organ.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指魁梧体格带来的肌肉力量；它指力量而非器官。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin diminutive, the real Greek double meaning, and real medical compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁指小形式、真实的希腊语双重含义，以及真实的医学术语组合。

normal.en: Latin musculus is a diminutive of mus mouse, and Greek mys has the same double meaning of mouse and muscle.
normal.cn: 拉丁 musculus 是 mus「老鼠」的指小形式，希腊 mys 也有老鼠与肌肉的双重含义。

normal.en: The adjective is muscular and the collective noun is musculature; neither is a plural of muscle.
normal.cn: 形容词是 muscular，集合名词是 musculature；两者都不是 muscle 的复数。

normal.en: Skeletal muscle is voluntary, smooth muscle is involuntary, cardiac muscle is involuntary and rhythmic.
normal.cn: 骨骼肌受意志控制，平滑肌不受控制，心肌不受控制而有节律。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the meanings: muscle mass and muscle fiber are tissue; muscle memory and show muscle are figurative.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分了词义：muscle mass 与 muscle fiber 指组织；muscle memory 与 show muscle 是比喻。

normal.en: The same tissue is called brawn when the point is strength and sinew when the point is the cord.
normal.cn: 当重点在力量时同一组织被称为 brawn，当重点在索带时则称 sinew。

abstract.en: Picture a rope that shortens by itself, and the bone tied to it must follow.
abstract.cn: 想象一根会自己缩短的绳子，被它系住的骨头只能跟着动。

abstract.en: Picture a small animal moving under a cloth: that is the old image behind the Latin name.
abstract.cn: 想象布下有一只小动物在移动：这正是那个拉丁名称背后的古老形象。

abstract.en: Picture influence as a hand pressing on a door: political muscle is the same gesture without a body.
abstract.cn: 想象影响力是一只压住门的手：政治实力就是同一个动作，只是不再有身体。

examples.en: Regular training increases both muscle mass and muscle strength.
examples.cn: 规律训练既能增加肌肉量，也能提高肌力。

examples.en: The diaphragm is a sheet of muscle that drives every breath.
examples.cn: 膈是一层肌肉，驱动每一次呼吸。

examples.en: The company flexed its financial muscle to buy out its rival.
examples.cn: 这家公司展示财力，收购了对手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马搜」（muscle）——马拉车靠的是一束束能收紧的绳索 → 肌肉

root: 拉丁 musculus「小老鼠」，为 mus「老鼠」的指小形式；一般认为皮下鼓动的肌肉被比作布下跑动的老鼠。希腊语 mys 兼指老鼠与肌肉，祖词为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one action: fibres shorten and pull. The action is then named as tissue, as a single organ, as three tissue types, as bodily force, as social pressure, as national power, and finally as memory stored in movement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都建立在一个动作上：纤维缩短并拉动。这个动作依次被命名为组织、单块器官、三种组织类型、身体力量、社会压力、国家实力，最后是储存在动作里的记忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bundles of rope that shorten on command and drag whatever they are tied to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束束听令缩短的绳索，把系住的东西拖着走。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND UNIT: the tissue as material, and one named bundle as an organ.
branches.cn: 材料与单位：作为材料的组织，以及作为器官的一块有名称的肌束。

branches.en: CONTROL TYPES: smooth muscle works unseen, cardiac muscle works without pause.
branches.cn: 控制类型：平滑肌在暗处工作，心肌不停歇地工作。

branches.en: SKILL AND FORCE: strength that moves a piano, and skill that moves without thought.
branches.cn: 力量与技能：能搬动钢琴的力气，以及不经思考就能完成的技能。

branches.en: SHOWN POWER: strength displayed to deter rivals.
branches.cn: 向外展示的力量：为震慑对手而摆出的实力。

branches.en: The bridge between body and politics: the same verb put muscle behind works for both.
branches.cn: 身体与政治的桥梁：同一个搭配 put muscle behind 对两者都适用。

intro.en: Muscle is a Latin diminutive, so its ending -culus is a suffix of smallness rather than a meaningful root; the modern family grows from the stem muscul-.
intro.cn: muscle 是拉丁指小词，结尾 -culus 是表示「小」的后缀而非有实义的词根；现代词族由词干 muscul- 生长出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin musculus and its root mus give the English family muscular, musculature and muscularity; the Greek doublet mys explains why the same image appears in both languages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 musculus 及其词根 mus 衍生英语的 muscular、musculature、muscularity；希腊语中的对应词 mys 说明两种语言为何出现同一形象。

items.example: The root is the ordinary Latin word for a mouse.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是拉丁语中表示老鼠的普通名词。

items.example: Musculus is literally a little mouse.
Latin anatomy named the moving flesh musculus.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁解剖学把会鼓动的肉称为 musculus。

items.example: Muscular tissue responds to nerve signals.
items.exampleCN: 肌肉组织对神经信号作出反应。

items.example: The athlete has a powerful musculature.
items.exampleCN: 这名运动员肌肉系统强健。

items.example: Judges score muscularity as well as leanness.
items.exampleCN: 裁判既看精瘦程度，也看肌肉发达程度。

items.meaning: a heavily built man, often hired as a guard or thug
items.meaningCN: 体格魁梧的男子，常受雇充当打手
items.example: Two musclemen stood at the door.

items.meaning: relating to the link between nerves and muscles
items.meaningCN: 与神经和肌肉连接有关的
items.example: The neuromuscular junction passes the signal across.
items.exampleCN: 神经肌肉接头把信号传递过去。

items.meaning: inside a muscle, as an injection
items.meaningCN: 肌肉内部的，如肌肉注射
items.example: The vaccine was given by an intramuscular injection.
items.exampleCN: 疫苗通过肌肉注射给药。

definition_en: thin cord used for tying, a series of similar things, or a cord that makes sound in an instrument
core_image: 一根细线从针眼穿过，把散落的东西串在一起
scene: 她用一根细绳把包裹捆好。 She tied the parcel with a piece of string.
sceneCN: 这里 string 是「细绳」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她用一根细绳把包裹捆好。

senses.title: Thin cord
senses.definition: thin cord used to tie things
senses.definitionCN: 用来捆东西的细绳
senses.example: She tied the parcel with a piece of string.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一根细绳把包裹捆好。
senses.why: This is the cord in your hand.
senses.whyCN: 这是拿在手里的绳子。

senses.title: A series
senses.definition: a number of similar things in a line or series
senses.definitionCN: 排成一列或一连串的同类事物
senses.example: A string of lights hung across the street.
senses.exampleCN: 一串灯横挂在街道上方。
senses.why: Things on a cord become things in a row.
senses.whyCN: 串在绳上的东西，变成了一列。

senses.title: A musical cord
senses.definition: a tight cord on an instrument that makes sound
senses.definitionCN: 乐器上振动发声的绷紧的线
senses.example: One string of the guitar broke.
senses.exampleCN: 吉他的一根弦断了。
senses.why: Sound is made by a stretched cord.
senses.whyCN: 声音由绷紧的弦发出。

intro.en: String comes from Old English streng, a cord.
intro.cn: string 来自古英语 streng，意为绳。

items.en: Streng meant a cord or rope.
items.cn: streng 指绳或索。

items.en: The root named a twisted line.
items.cn: 这个词根表示搓成的线。

items.en: String named a thin cord.
items.cn: 中古英语 string 指细绳。

items.en: A string of things meant a series.
items.cn: a string of things 表示一连串事物。

items.en: Instrument strings gave string its musical sense.
items.cn: 乐器上的弦赋予了 string 音乐含义。

note.en: String is compared with look-alike words and with words for cord.
note.cn: 把 string 与形近词以及表示绳线的词作比较。

entries.definition: having great power
entries.definitionCN: 强壮的

entries.definition: the season after winter
entries.definitionCN: 春天

entries.definition: to remove a covering
entries.definitionCN: 剥去

entries.definition: a thick strong cord
entries.definitionCN: 粗绳

entries.definition: a very thin line of cotton
entries.definitionCN: 线

entries.definition: a thin rope
entries.definitionCN: 细绳

normalIntro.en: String is a line that ties, lines up, or sings.
normalIntro.cn: string 是一根能捆、能串、能唱的线。

normal.en: She cut the string with scissors.
normal.cn: 她用剪刀剪断了绳子。

normal.en: A string of buses waited outside.
normal.cn: 外面排着一串公交车。

normal.en: He plays a string instrument.
normal.cn: 他演奏弦乐器。

normal.en: She pulled strings to get the job.
normal.cn: 她走后门得到了这份工作。

normal.en: They offered help with no strings attached.
normal.cn: 他们提供帮助，不附带条件。

abstract.en: A string is a promise stretched between two points.
abstract.cn: 一根绳，是两点之间拉紧的承诺。

abstract.en: Small things become a story when strung together.
abstract.cn: 小东西串起来，就成了故事。

abstract.en: Even a thin string can make a sound.
abstract.cn: 再细的弦，也能发出声音。

examples.en: She tied the parcel with a piece of string.
examples.cn: 她用一根细绳把包裹捆好。

examples.en: A string of lights hung across the street.
examples.cn: 一串灯横挂在街道上方。

examples.en: One string of the guitar broke.
examples.cn: 吉他的一根弦断了。

dict_mnemonic.text: string 是「细绳」；把东西串在绳上成了一串，把绳绷在乐器上成了弦，暗地里牵绳就是走后门。

root: 来自古英语 streng（绳、索），属日耳曼语词，本指搓成的线；由实物的细绳，引申为一串事物，再指乐器上发声的弦。

sensesIntro.en: String is cord you tie with, a row of things, or a cord that sings.
sensesIntro.cn: string 是拿来捆的绳、排成一串的东西，或会唱歌的弦。

core.en: A thin line pulled through a parcel.
core.cn: 一根穿过包裹的细线。

branches.en: A parcel is tied shut.
branches.cn: 包裹被捆好。

branches.en: Lights hang one after another.
branches.cn: 灯一盏接一盏地挂着。

branches.en: A finger presses a guitar string.
branches.cn: 手指按住吉他弦。

branches.en: The cord turns separate things into a row.
branches.cn: 绳子把分散的东西变成一列。

branches.en: A row of notes hangs on a string.
branches.cn: 一串音符挂在弦上。

intro.en: String forms a plural and adjectives about texture and music.
intro.cn: string 有复数，并能构成表示质地与音乐的形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: A harp is a stringed instrument.
The violin is a string instrument.
He pulled strings for his son.
The gift had no strings attached.

definition_zh: 视力；视觉；视野；想象、眼光；幻象、景象；远见
definition_en: the ability to see; an idea of what something could be like in the future; something you imagine seeing
core_image: 一双眼睛：既能看清眼前，也能望向别人还看不见的远方
scene: 画家站在山顶，画纸上还没有任何颜色。 She closed her eyes and described the city of her vision.
sceneCN: 这里 vision 是「想象中的图景、愿景」（第 4 个义项：构想中的未来图景）；句意是她闭上眼睛，描述她想象中的那座城市。先看清，再望远，就是这个词。

pos.zh: 名词：视力；视觉；视野；想象；幻象；远见

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「视觉的」，由同根形容词构成
形容词，义为「有远见的」，也可作名词指「有远见的人」
动词，义为「设想、展望」，由 en- 加同根词构成
名词，义为「电视」，由 tele-（远）加同根词构成

senses.title: The ability to see
senses.titleCN: 视力：用眼睛感知的能力
senses.definition: the ability of the eyes to see things
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛看见东西的能力
senses.example: Her vision blurred after hours at the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 盯着屏幕几个小时后，她的视力变得模糊。
senses.why: Latin videre means to see; the noun names the very capacity of seeing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 videre 意为看；这个名词指称「看」这一能力本身。

senses.title: Sight as experience
senses.titleCN: 视觉：所见之物与观看体验
senses.definition: the sense or experience of seeing, or something that is seen
senses.definitionCN: 观看这一感知方式，或被看见的东西
senses.example: The cathedral is a vision of white stone against the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 这座大教堂是映衬在天空下的一幅白色石头的视觉景象。
senses.why: What the eye receives becomes the content of seeing; hence a striking sight.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛接收的内容就是「看」的素材，引申为引人注目的景象。

senses.title: Range of sight
senses.definition: the area that you can see from one place or position
senses.definitionCN: 从某一位置能看到的空间范围
senses.example: The bird slipped out of my field of vision.
senses.exampleCN: 那只鸟滑出了我的视野。
senses.why: Seeing has edges; the word maps the boundary of what is visible.
senses.whyCN: 「看」有边界，这个词标出可见范围的两端。

senses.title: An imagined picture
senses.titleCN: 想象：构想中的图景或愿景
senses.definition: an idea or mental picture of what something could become
senses.definitionCN: 对某物未来样子的构想或心理图景
senses.example: She closed her eyes and described the city of her vision.
senses.exampleCN: 她闭上眼睛，描述她想象中的那座城市。
senses.why: The mind's eye sees too; an inner picture extends sight beyond the present.
senses.whyCN: 心灵的眼睛也会「看」，内心的画面把视线延伸到当下之外。

senses.title: Foresight and judgment
senses.definition: the quality of planning or thinking wisely about the future
senses.definitionCN: 对未来做出明智规划的洞察力
senses.example: He rebuilt the school with vision and patience.
senses.exampleCN: 他以远见和耐心重建了这所学校。
senses.why: One who sees far ahead leads; imagination about the future becomes wisdom.
senses.whyCN: 能提前看见的人才能引领，对未来的想象升华为判断力。

senses.title: A dream seen as real
senses.titleCN: 幻象：梦中或恍惚间所见的景象
senses.definition: something seen in a dream or trance as if it were real
senses.definitionCN: 在梦、幻觉或宗教体验中仿佛真实看见的景象
senses.example: In the story, the prophet receives a night vision.
senses.exampleCN: 故事里，先知在夜间见到一个异象。
senses.why: An inner picture can feel as vivid as eyesight, even when asleep.
senses.whyCN: 内心的画面可以像亲眼所见一样鲜明，甚至在睡梦中。

senses.title: Clear insight
senses.definition: the ability to perceive clearly what is true or important
senses.definitionCN: 清楚看出真相或要点的能力
senses.example: Her memoir shows rare vision about her own past.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回忆录对自己的过去表现出罕见的洞察。
senses.why: Clear seeing turns into clear understanding; sight is a metaphor for knowing.
senses.whyCN: 看得清楚转化为想得透彻，「看」成为「懂」的隐喻。

senses.title: A haunting image
senses.titleCN: 浮现的影像：萦绕心头的画面
senses.definition: a vivid picture that appears suddenly in the mind, especially one that troubles you
senses.definitionCN: 突然出现在脑海里、尤其令人不安的鲜活画面
senses.example: He could not erase the vision of the empty house.
senses.exampleCN: 他无法抹去那栋空房子的影像。
senses.why: Memory replays an inner picture uninvited; seeing again without the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 记忆不请自来地重播内心画面，不用眼睛却像再次看见。

intro.en: Vision descends from Latin videre, to see, through the noun visio, the act or fact of seeing.
intro.cn: vision 源自拉丁语 videre（看），经名词 visio（看见的行为或事实）传入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *weid- means to see or to know, giving both sight and knowledge words across many languages.
items.cn: 重构词根 *weid- 意为看或知晓，在许多语言中同时衍生出「视」与「知」两族词。

items.en: Videre means to see; the derived noun visio means the act of seeing or a thing seen.
items.cn: 拉丁语 videre 意为看；派生名词 visio 意为看见的行为或所见之物。

items.en: The word enters French as vision, keeping both the physical and the imagined senses.
items.cn: 该词以 vision 进入法语，同时保留字面所见与想象所见两义。

items.en: English borrows vision in religious contexts first, meaning something seen in a dream or revelation.
items.cn: 英语最初在宗教语境借用 vision，指梦中或启示中所见的景象。

items.en: The ordinary sense of eyesight becomes established in English medical and everyday writing.
items.cn: 15 世纪，「视力」这一日常义在医学与日常文本中确立。

items.en: Vision now spans eyesight, imagination, and leadership, from blurry vision to a corporate vision statement.
items.cn: 如今 vision 涵盖视力、想象与领导远见，从视力模糊到企业愿景皆用此词。

note.en: Vision sits beside sight, sight-words, and dream-words; look-alikes share the Latin root, near meanings share the field of seeing and imagining.
note.cn: vision 与 sight、同根 see 族词、梦幻词相邻：形近组共享拉丁词根，近义组共享「看与想象」义场。

entries.definition: relating to seeing or the eyes
entries.definitionCN: 视觉的、用眼睛的；与 vision 同根的形容词

entries.definition: having or showing clear ideas about the future; a person with such ideas
entries.definitionCN: 有远见的（人）；由 vision 派生的形容词与名词

entries.definition: the act of dividing or the result of dividing
entries.definitionCN: 分开、分割；与 vision 拼写相近且同为 -sion 结尾，但词根不同，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a form or variant of something
entries.definitionCN: 版本、变体；同以 -sion 结尾，词根是 vertere（转），与 vision 词源不同

entries.definition: a face or appearance, especially in literary use
entries.definitionCN: 面容、外观；同出拉丁 videre 词族，属文学用词

entries.definition: the ability to see, or something that is seen
entries.definitionCN: 视力、景象；日耳曼词源的近义词，偏日常

entries.definition: the ability of the eyes to see
entries.definitionCN: 视力；只指生理能力，不含远义

entries.definition: a false idea or image that seems real
entries.definitionCN: 错觉、幻象；与幻象义相邻，但强调「假」

entries.definition: a series of images in sleep, or a strong hope
entries.definitionCN: 梦、梦想；与想象义相邻，偏愿望

entries.definition: the ability to see what will happen and prepare for it
entries.definitionCN: 预见、深谋远虑；与远见义相邻，强调提前防备

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Latin root videre, to see, and its real word family.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自拉丁词根 videre（看）及其真实词族。

normal.en: videre means to see; vision is literally the act of seeing.
normal.cn: videre 意为看；vision 字面就是「看的行为」。

normal.en: television lets you see across distance: tele- plus the same root.
normal.cn: television 让你看到远处：tele-（远）加同一词根。

normal.en: visual describes anything seen with the eyes.
normal.cn: visual 描述一切用眼睛看到的东西。

normal.en: envision is to see a plan inside your head before building it.
normal.cn: envision 是在动工之前先在脑中「看见」方案。

normal.en: visionary names a person who sees what others cannot yet see.
normal.cn: visionary 指能看见别人尚看不见之事的人。

abstract.en: Picture two lights in one eye: one for what is here, one for what could be.
abstract.cn: 想象眼睛里有两盏灯：一盏照亮眼前，一盏照向可能。

abstract.en: A fog lifts and the road ahead appears: that clearing is vision at work.
abstract.cn: 雾散路现：那片豁然开朗，正是 vision 在工作。

abstract.en: The mind's eye opens in the dark and draws a city that does not exist yet.
abstract.cn: 心灵的眼睛在黑暗中睁开，画出一座尚不存在的城。

examples.en: Years of night shifts slowly damaged his vision.
examples.cn: 多年的夜班慢慢损害了他的视力。

examples.en: The founder's vision was a library open to everyone in the city.
examples.cn: 创始人的构想是一座对全城开放的图书馆。

examples.en: A tall figure appeared at the edge of her vision and then was gone.
examples.cn: 一个高大的身影出现在她视野边缘，随即消失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「未整」——视力未整理好就看不清；远见是把未来的图景先「未雨绸缪地整」出来。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自拉丁 videre（看）。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看）+ 名词后缀构成 visio（看见的行为），经古法语 vision 进入英语。词根 *weid- 重构形式，同时衍生出 wit（智力）、view、evident 等词；「视」与「知」同源。

sensesIntro.en: From the eyes' power outward: sight, what is seen, the range of seeing, and finally the mind's eye that pictures the future.
sensesIntro.cn: 从眼睛的能力向外铺开：视力、所见之物、看的范围，最后到心灵的眼睛对未来构图的远见。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one act of seeing, from the eye outward to the mind
core.cn: 核心意象：同一次「看」，从眼睛延伸到心灵

branches.en: The physical act and its raw result
branches.cn: 生理之看及其直接产物：视力与景象

branches.en: Sight with boundaries: the field you can cover
branches.cn: 有边界的看：目光覆盖的视野

branches.en: Seeing without eyes: imagined, dreamed, or haunting pictures
branches.cn: 不用眼睛的看：想象、梦境与萦绕的画面

branches.en: Seeing turned wise: foresight and clear judgment
branches.cn: 看升华为智：远见与洞察

branches.en: Foresight fixed into a plan becomes a guiding purpose
branches.cn: 远见落成蓝图，便成为引领方向的目标

intro.en: The family of Latin videre spreads through prefixes that move the act of seeing toward, back, apart, or out.
intro.cn: videre 词族借助前缀把「看」引向不同方向：向前、向后、分开、向外。

latinIntro.en: In Latin, videre and its prefixed verbs built a dense family of seeing-words.
latinIntro.cn: 在拉丁语中，videre 及其前缀动词构成了密集的「看」义词族。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 寡妇，字面为「被留下独自看顾的人」

derivatives.zh: 视觉的，由同根形容词构成
有远见的，由 vision 加后缀构成
设想，由 en- 加 vision 构成

definition_en: to identify someone or something as known; to admit a fact; to give credit or approval; to match a pattern by machine
core_image: 街上有人叫住你，你回头认出是老同学
scene: 街上有人叫住你，你回头看了两秒才认出对方。 I did not recognize him until he called my name.
sceneCN: 这里 recognize 是「认出」（第 1 个义项：认出认识的人或物）；句意为直到他叫我的名字，我才认出他。画面里可留意：回头张望、叫住你的那只手。

senses.title: To know someone again
senses.definition: to identify a person or a thing as one already known
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物辨认出为已知对象
senses.example: I did not recognize him until he called my name.
senses.exampleCN: 直到他叫我的名字，我才认出他。
senses.why: Recognoscere meant to know again, and the English verb keeps that moment of a second meeting.
senses.whyCN: recognoscere 意为「再一次认识」，英语动词保留了「第二次相遇」的瞬间。

senses.title: To admit a fact
senses.definition: to accept that something is true, often reluctantly
senses.definitionCN: 接受某事为真，常带不情愿
senses.example: The government finally recognized the problem.
senses.exampleCN: 政府终于承认了这个问题。
senses.why: To know again is also to admit what one already knew, so the word covers reluctant acceptance.
senses.whyCN: 「再一次知道」也是承认自己早已知道的事，因此这个词涵盖不情愿的接受。

senses.title: To give credit
senses.definition: to show appreciation for a person's work or value
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的工作或价值表示欣赏
senses.example: Her work was recognized by the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 她的工作得到了委员会的认可。
senses.why: When others know a person's worth again and again, that knowing becomes public credit.
senses.whyCN: 当他人一次次看见某个人的价值，这种认识就成了公开的认可。

senses.title: To match a pattern by machine
senses.definition: to identify a face, a voice, or a shape by computer
senses.definitionCN: 由计算机辨认面孔、声音或形状
senses.example: The app can recognize handwriting.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用能识别人手写的字。
senses.why: A machine that matches a pattern knows it again, so the old verb fits the new technology.
senses.whyCN: 能匹配图案的机器，就是「再一次认出」它，于是旧动词恰好适用于新技术。

intro.en: Recognize is the Latin verb of knowing again, carried through French and given an English spelling.
intro.cn: recognize 是拉丁语「再一次认识」的动词，经法语传来，并换上英语拼写。

items.en: Cognoscere meant to know or learn, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: cognoscere 意为认识或得知，是整个词族的词根。

items.en: Recognoscere added re-, again, giving the sense of knowing a second time.
items.cn: recognoscere 加上 re-（再次），得到「第二次认识」。

items.en: Old French carried the verb into English with the same re- prefix.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带入英语，re- 前缀保持不变。

items.en: Middle English recognizen covered both identifying and admitting.
items.cn: 中古英语 recognizen 既指辨认，也指承认。

items.en: American spelling settled on -ize, while British English also accepts -ise.
items.cn: 美式拼写定为 -ize，英式英语也接受 -ise。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of identifying and approving.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾音相同的动词；近义组收表辨认与认可的词。

entries.definition: To arrange something in a new way.
entries.definitionCN: 重组；重新安排。

entries.definition: To become aware of something.
entries.definitionCN: 意识到；实现。

entries.definition: To judge faults in something.
entries.definitionCN: 批评。

entries.definition: To say what something is.
entries.definitionCN: 辨认；确认。

entries.definition: To admit or thank.
entries.definitionCN: 承认；致谢。

entries.definition: To accept a truth unwillingly.
entries.definitionCN: 承认。

entries.definition: To recognize the value of something.
entries.definitionCN: 欣赏；重视。

normalIntro.en: The word is knowing plus again, and the same act covers a face, a fact, a person's value, and a pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「知道」加「再一次」，同一个行为覆盖一张脸、一个事实、一个人的价值，以及一段图案。

normal.en: Recognize is cognition with a re- in front and an -ize on the end.
normal.cn: recognize 就是 cognition 前面加 re-，后面加 -ize。

normal.en: Recognize a face is the picture; recognize a fact is the extension.
normal.cn: recognize a face 是画面，recognize a fact 是引申。

normal.en: Widely recognized is a common phrase on a plaque or a report.
normal.cn: widely recognized 是奖牌或报告上的常见说法。

normal.en: British English also writes recognise, with s instead of z.
normal.cn: 英式英语也写作 recognise，用 s 代替 z。

normal.en: Do not drop the g: recognize, recognized, recognizing.
normal.cn: 不要漏掉 g：recognize、recognized、recognizing。

abstract.en: To recognize is to let the past prove that it still lives.
abstract.cn: 认出，就是让过去证明它仍然活着。

abstract.en: Recognizing a fault is the first honest act a person can perform.
abstract.cn: 承认错误，是一个人能做的第一件诚实之事。

abstract.en: The one who recognizes another gives that person a place in the world.
abstract.cn: 认出他人的人，等于给了对方一个在世界上的一席之地。

examples.en: I did not recognize him until he called my name.
examples.cn: 直到他叫我的名字，我才认出他。

examples.en: The government finally recognized the problem.
examples.cn: 政府终于承认了这个问题。

examples.en: The app can recognize handwriting.
examples.cn: 这款应用能识别人手写的字。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）加 cognize（认识）：再认识一次，就是认出；把已知的事实再确认，就是承认。

root: 拉丁 cognoscere（认识）→ recognoscere（再认识）→ 中古英语 recognizen → 英语 recognize；同族有 recognition、recognizable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is knowing again; the senses move from a face to a fact, to public credit, and to a machine match.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「再一次认识」；义项从一张脸，到事实，到公开认可，再到机器匹配。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stranger calling your name, and a face becoming familiar.
core.cn: 核心意象：陌生人叫出你的名字，一张脸忽然变得熟悉。

branches.en: a face turning in the street
branches.cn: 街上一张转过来的脸

branches.en: a report admitting a fault
branches.cn: 一份承认过错的报告

branches.en: a prize handed over
branches.cn: 递到手上的奖

branches.en: an app reading handwriting
branches.cn: 应用读出手写的字

branches.en: a person known and a person honoured
branches.cn: 认出一个也表彰一个人

intro.en: The Latin verb of knowing takes a prefix of repetition and an English verb ending, and the spellings vary by region.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「认识」动词接上表重复的前缀与英语动词词尾，拼写因地区而异。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is cognoscere, and re- marks the second knowing; the ending -ize came through French and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 cognoscere，re- 标记第二次认识；词尾 -ize 经法语与英语形成。

definition_zh: 在别处；到别处；在其他地方
definition_en: in or to another place; in other places generally
core_image: 目光越过眼前这块地方，落在远处的另一片区域
scene: 聚会散场后，主人把多余的椅子搬到别处。 The extra chairs were carried elsewhere after the party.
sceneCN: 这里 elsewhere 是「到别处」（第 01 个义项：到另一个地方）；句意是聚会结束后多余的椅子被搬到了别处。

pos.zh: 副词：在别处；到别处；在其他地方

derivatives.zh: 复合成分，义为「别的」，与 where 合成 elsewhere
复合成分，义为「哪里」，与 else 合成 elsewhere

senses.title: In or to another place
senses.definition: in or to a different place from the one already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 在或到一个不同于已提及地点的地方
senses.example: The extra chairs were carried elsewhere after the party.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会结束后，多余的椅子被搬到了别处。
senses.why: Else supplies the idea of another and where supplies place, so elsewhere is simply the place that is not here.
senses.whyCN: else 提供「另一个」的意思，where 提供「地方」，所以 elsewhere 就是那个不在这里的地方。

senses.title: In other places in general
senses.definition: in other places, considered as a group rather than one specific place
senses.definitionCN: 泛指其他多个地方，而不是某一个具体地点
senses.example: Elsewhere in Europe, the rule is stricter.
senses.exampleCN: 在欧洲其他地方，这条规定更严格。
senses.why: The same compound can widen from one other place to any other place, so the word also serves as a general contrast.
senses.whyCN: 同一个复合词可以从「另一个地方」扩大到「任何其他地方」，于是它也用来作总体对比。

senses.title: In another source or part of a text
senses.titleCN: 在别处（指其他来源或篇章）
senses.definition: in another part of a book, report or set of records
senses.definitionCN: 在同一本书、报告或记录的其他部分
senses.example: The report refers elsewhere for the full figures.
senses.exampleCN: 完整数据报告让读者去别处查看。
senses.why: A text is treated as a space with places, so a cross-reference sends the reader to a different spot in that space.
senses.whyCN: 文本被当成一个有地点可走的空间，于是交叉引用就是把读者送到这个空间里的另一处。

intro.en: Elsewhere is a transparent compound of else and where, already present in Old English.
intro.cn: elsewhere 是 else 与 where 的透明复合词，古英语中已经存在。

items.en: The compound appears as elleshwær, meaning in another place.
items.cn: 古英语作 elleshwær，意为「在另一个地方」。

items.en: Spelling passed through elleswhere and elsquer.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写经过 elleswhere、elsquer 等形式。

items.en: Printing helped fix the modern spelling elsewhere.
items.cn: 印刷术帮助固定了现代拼写 elsewhere。

items.en: The word extended from physical places to sources and parts of texts.
items.cn: 这个词从物理地点扩展到资料来源与文本部分。

items.en: It is now a standard adverb in news, law and academic writing.
items.cn: 如今它是新闻、法律与学术写作中的标准副词。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the else and where building blocks; the near-meaning group places elsewhere among other place words.
note.cn: 形近组展示 else 与 where 这两块构件；近义组把 elsewhere 放进其他地点词中比较。

entries.definition: The other element that supplies the idea of another.
entries.definitionCN: 复合成分，提供「另一个」的意思。

entries.definition: The element that supplies place.
entries.definitionCN: 复合成分，提供「地方」的意思。

entries.definition: In all places, built with the same place element.
entries.definitionCN: 同样带 -where 的地点词，义为「到处」。

entries.definition: In or to an unspecified place.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在某处」，地点同样不确定。

entries.definition: In or to a foreign country.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在国外」，是 elsewhere 的一种具体化。

entries.definition: At a distance from the current place.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「离开、在远处」，强调距离。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split elsewhere into else plus where, then move the reader from one room to another.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 elsewhere 拆成 else 加 where，再把读者从一个房间带到另一个房间。

normal.en: Else plus where means the other place.
normal.cn: else 加 where 就是「另一个地方」。

normal.en: If it is not here, look elsewhere.
normal.cn: 如果不在这里，就到别处找。

normal.en: Elsewhere in Europe marks a wider contrast.
normal.cn: elsewhere in Europe 表示更大范围的对比。

normal.en: A cross-reference sends you elsewhere in the book.
normal.cn: 交叉引用把你送到书里的别处。

normal.en: Everywhere and somewhere share the same -where.
normal.cn: everywhere 与 somewhere 都带同一个 -where。

abstract.en: Picture a spotlight leaving this room and landing on another.
abstract.cn: 想象一束聚光灯离开这个房间，落到另一个房间。

abstract.en: The word is a small map with only two points: here and not here.
abstract.cn: 这个词像一张只有两个点的小地图：这里，和不在这里。

abstract.en: A footnote is elsewhere made visible.
abstract.cn: 脚注就是被标出来的「别处」。

examples.en: The extra chairs were carried elsewhere after the party.
examples.cn: 聚会结束后，多余的椅子被搬到了别处。

examples.en: Elsewhere in Europe, the rule is stricter.
examples.cn: 在欧洲其他地方，这条规定更严格。

examples.en: The report refers elsewhere for the full figures.
examples.cn: 完整数据报告让读者去别处查看。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱尔斯维尔」——不是这儿，是别的哪儿

root: 由 else（别的）与 where（哪里）复合而成，古英语作 elleshwær，字面就是「在另一个地方」。

sensesIntro.en: Elsewhere begins as one other place, widens to other places in general, and then enters texts as another source.
sensesIntro.cn: elsewhere 从某一个别处开始，扩大到泛指其他地方，再进入文本表示另一个出处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gaze sliding past the present spot to a distant one.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光越过眼前的位置，滑向远处另一处。

branches.en: THE OTHER SPOT: a specific place that is not here.
branches.cn: 另一处：一个具体但不在这里的地点。

branches.en: THE WIDER WORLD: other places taken together.
branches.cn: 更广的世界：把其他地方合起来看。

branches.en: THE TEXT: another page or source.
branches.cn: 文本线：另一页或另一个来源。

branches.en: ONE AND MANY: one other place can widen into many.
branches.cn: 一与多：一个别处可以扩大成许多别处。

branches.en: SPACE AND PAGE: a place word becomes a reading direction.
branches.cn: 空间与书页：地点词变成了阅读方向。

intro.en: Elsewhere is a compound of two free morphemes, else and where, with no classical prefix.
intro.cn: elsewhere 由 else 与 where 两个自由语素复合而成，没有古典前缀。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Germanic, so there is no Latin entry to list.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都属于日耳曼语层，因此没有可列的拉丁词条。

items.example: It appears in everywhere and somewhere.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 everywhere 与 somewhere 中。
它由 else 与 where 合成。

definition_en: a group of sports teams that compete against one another, an alliance of states or groups, and an older verb meaning to unite in such an alliance
core_image: 一排球队队旗插在同一块场地上，旗与旗之间用绳子系在一起
scene: 赛季开始前，球迷在球场外排起长队。 Their team finished top of the league last season.
sceneCN: 这里 league 指「联赛」（第 1 个义项）；句意为他们的球队上赛季排名联赛榜首。图中可辨识物件：队旗、球场看台、积分榜。

derivatives.zh: 由 league 与 table 复合，指联赛积分榜
由 non- 加 league 构成，指不属于职业联赛的
league 的复数形式，也可指很远的距离，如 leagues away

senses.title: A group of teams competing against each other
senses.definition: an organized group of sports clubs or teams that play against one another for a title
senses.definitionCN: 为争夺冠军而相互比赛的有组织的体育俱乐部或队伍
senses.example: Their team finished top of the league last season.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的球队上赛季排名联赛榜首。
senses.why: A league was first a group bound by an agreement, and teams bound into a fixture list are exactly that: a set of rivals tied to the same schedule.
senses.whyCN: league 最初指由协议绑在一起的一群人，而被赛程绑在一起的球队正是如此：一群被同一张日程拴住的对手。

senses.title: An alliance of states or groups
senses.definition: an association of countries, parties or groups formed to act together
senses.definitionCN: 为共同行动而组成的国家、政党或团体联合体
senses.example: Several small states formed a league to protect their trade routes.
senses.exampleCN: 几个小国结成联盟以保护各自的贸易路线。
senses.why: Latin ligare means to bind, so the political sense is the literal one: separate parties tied by a treaty into one body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ligare 意为捆绑，所以政治义才是字面义：彼此独立的各方被条约绑成一个整体。

senses.title: To unite in an alliance
senses.definition: to join together with others in an alliance, now mainly literary or historical
senses.definitionCN: 与他人联合结成同盟，现在多用于文学或历史叙述
senses.example: The border towns leagued together against the raiders.
senses.exampleCN: 边境各镇联合起来对抗入侵者。
senses.why: If a league is a body bound together, then to league is simply to enter that binding, which is why the verb mirrors the noun.
senses.whyCN: 如果 league 是被绑在一起的整体，那么 to league 就是加入这次捆绑，因此动词与名词完全对应。

intro.en: League comes from a Latin verb meaning to bind, by way of Italian and French, so an alliance is literally a tying together.
intro.cn: league 经意大利语和法语来自拉丁语中意为「捆绑」的动词，所以同盟字面上就是「绑在一起」。

items.en: Ligare meant to bind or tie, and a league was first a binding together of people.
items.cn: ligare 意为捆绑、结合，而 league 最初指把人们绑在一起。

items.en: Italian lega named an alliance, a group bound by an agreement.
items.cn: 意大利语 lega 指同盟，即由协议绑在一起的一群人。

items.en: Old French ligue carried the political sense of a confederacy into English.
items.cn: 古法语 ligue 把「邦联、同盟」这一政治含义带进英语。

items.en: Middle English league named an alliance of rulers, and by the sixteenth century it also named a group of sports sides.
items.cn: 中古英语 league 指统治者之间的同盟，到十六世纪也指一组体育队伍。

items.en: Modern English keeps the alliance sense in phrases such as in league with, while the sports sense dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 现代英语在 in league with 等说法中保留同盟义，体育运动义则主导日常使用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and compounds of league; the near-meaning group collects other words for an alliance.
note.cn: 形近组收 league 的形式与复合词；近义组收其他表示同盟的词。

entries.definition: The plural of league, for several competitions or alliances.
entries.definitionCN: league 的复数，指多个联赛或同盟。

entries.definition: The past form, meaning formed an alliance.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式，意为结成了同盟。

entries.definition: Outside the professional league system, used of smaller clubs.
entries.definitionCN: 不属于职业联赛体系的，用于较小的俱乐部。

entries.definition: A formal agreement to work together.
entries.definitionCN: 正式约定共同行动的联盟。

entries.definition: A temporary union of parties or groups.
entries.definitionCN: 政党或团体组成的临时联合。

entries.definition: A union of states or organizations with shared rules.
entries.definitionCN: 按共同规则组成的国家或组织联合体。

entries.definition: The act or state of being joined together.
entries.definitionCN: 联合的行为或状态。

normalIntro.en: The word means a binding, and both a treaty and a fixture list are ways of tying separate parties into one arrangement.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的意思是「捆绑」，而条约与赛程都是把彼此独立的一方绑进同一安排的方式。

normal.en: Latin ligare means to bind, so a league is people or teams tied together.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ligare 意为捆绑，所以 league 就是被绑在一起的人或球队。

normal.en: The League of Nations was literally a binding of states after a war.
normal.cn: 国际联盟字面上就是战后各国的一次捆绑。

normal.en: In league with somebody usually hints at a secret or dishonest binding.
normal.cn: in league with somebody 通常暗示一种秘密或不正当的勾结。

normal.en: A football league is a binding by schedule: every club must play every other.
normal.cn: 足球联赛是一种按赛程的捆绑：每个俱乐部都必须与其他俱乐部比赛。

normal.en: To league is the old verb for entering that alliance, now mostly literary.
normal.cn: to league 是表示加入同盟的旧动词，现在多用于文学。

abstract.en: Competition and alliance share one word because both require parties to accept the same set of obligations.
abstract.cn: 竞争与同盟共用一个词，因为两者都要求各方接受同一套义务。

abstract.en: A league is a promise made visible: the table, the fixture list, the treaty are its rope.
abstract.cn: 联赛是把承诺变得可见：积分榜、赛程、条约就是它的绳子。

abstract.en: To be in league is to be tied to someone, whether by trust or by guilt.
abstract.cn: 身处一个 league 就是与某人绑在一起，不论靠信任还是靠罪责。

examples.en: Their team finished top of the league last season.
examples.cn: 他们的球队上赛季排名联赛榜首。

examples.en: Several small states formed a league to protect their trade routes.
examples.cn: 几个小国结成联盟以保护各自的贸易路线。

examples.en: The border towns leagued together against the raiders.
examples.cn: 边境各镇联合起来对抗入侵者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离格」——离了格的球队被编进同一个联赛；谐音记住 league 是联赛、联盟。

root: 源自拉丁语 ligare（捆绑），经意大利语 lega 与古法语 ligue 进入英语；同盟本义即「绑在一起」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a binding of separate parties; it appears as a political alliance, a sporting competition and the old verb for joining one.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是把彼此独立的各方绑在一起；它表现为政治同盟、体育联赛，以及表示加入同盟的旧动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: club flags planted in one field, tied to each other with rope.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排队旗插在同一块场地上，旗与旗用绳子系在一起。

branches.en: envoys signing a treaty in a plain room
branches.cn: 使节在简朴的房间里签署条约

branches.en: small states joining to guard a trade road
branches.cn: 小国联合以守护贸易通道

branches.en: a table showing every club's points
branches.cn: 显示各俱乐部积分的积分榜

branches.en: a full stadium on a match day
branches.cn: 比赛日坐满的球场

branches.en: border towns swearing to stand together
branches.cn: 边境各镇宣誓共同抵御

intro.en: A Latin verb for binding passes through Italian and French, and English adds plural and compound forms to name competitions and alliances.
intro.cn: 一个表示捆绑的拉丁动词经意大利语与法语传来，英语又加复数与复合形式来命名联赛与同盟。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 棘手的；难对付的；狡猾的；诡计多端的
definition_en: something difficult to deal with and needing care or skill, or a person who deceives by tricks
core_image: 脚下一块湿滑的石头：看起来普通，踩上去才知道要格外小心
scene: 登山路上向导停下来指着前方提醒大家放慢脚步。 The guide stopped and said the next section of the path was tricky.
sceneCN: 这里 tricky 是「棘手的；难对付的」（第 1 个义项：难处理、需要小心的）；句意为向导提醒大家下一段路不好走。脚下那块湿滑的石头，就是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 棘手的；难对付的；需要小心的

collocations.zh: 敏感地带；容易出问题的话题

derivatives.zh: 由 tricky 加 -ly 构成，义为「狡猾地；靠花招地」
由 tricky 加 -ness 构成，义为「棘手；狡猾」

senses.title: Difficult to deal with
senses.definition: hard to handle or deal with, and needing care or skill
senses.definitionCN: 难以处理，需要小心或技巧的
senses.example: The guide stopped and said the next section of the path was tricky.
senses.exampleCN: 向导停下来，说下一段路不好走。
senses.why: A trick is a move that surprises you, so a tricky thing behaves in ways you did not expect and must be handled carefully.
senses.whyCN: trick 是让人措手不及的花招，所以棘手的事会以意想不到的方式给你出难题，必须小心应付。

senses.title: Likely to catch you out
senses.titleCN: 暗藏陷阱的；容易出错的
senses.definition: likely to deceive people or make them make mistakes
senses.definitionCN: 容易让人上当或出错的
senses.example: The second question was tricky because it looked simpler than it was.
senses.exampleCN: 第二道题很刁钻，因为看起来比实际简单。
senses.why: When a test sets tricks for you, the question itself becomes a trap, so tricky describes anything designed to catch you out.
senses.whyCN: 当题目里设了圈套，题目本身就成了陷阱，所以 tricky 形容一切暗藏机关、引人出错的东西。

senses.title: Clever at deceiving
senses.definition: clever at deceiving people or getting what one wants by tricks
senses.definitionCN: 善于欺骗他人或用花招达到目的的
senses.example: Everyone knew he was a tricky trader who hid the real price.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都知道他是个滑头商人，总把真实价格藏着掖着。
senses.why: A person full of tricks uses them on others, so the word moves from things to people who cannot be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 满脑子花招的人会把花招用在别人身上，于是这个词从「事情」转到「不可信的人」。

intro.en: Tricky is built directly on the noun trick, adding the adjective suffix -y to describe whatever involves tricks.
intro.cn: tricky 直接由名词 trick 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，形容一切与花招相关的性质。

items.en: The noun trick came from Old French trique, linked to triquier meaning to cheat or trick, generally thought to trace further back to the Vulgar Latin verb triccare.
items.cn: 名词 trick 来自古法语 trique，与动词 triquier（欺骗）相关，一般认为可再追溯到通俗拉丁语动词 triccare。

items.en: The reconstructed verb triccare is usually explained as meaning to trick or cheat, though its deeper origin remains uncertain.
items.cn: 重构形式 triccare 一般解释为「耍花招、欺骗」，其更深的来源并不确定。

items.en: Trick entered English in the fifteenth century, first meaning a fraud or a cheating act, later widened to any clever or playful move.
items.cn: trick 于十五世纪进入英语，最初指欺诈行为，后来扩大到任何机巧或玩笑式的动作。

items.en: The adjective tricky appeared in the eighteenth century, first describing deceitful people, then spreading to difficult tasks and situations.
items.cn: 形容词 tricky 出现于十八世纪，最初形容狡猾的人，后来扩展到困难的任务与局面。

items.en: In modern usage tricky most often means difficult to deal with, while the older sense of deceitful survives chiefly in informal speech.
items.cn: 现代用法中 tricky 多指「难对付的」，「狡猾的」旧义主要保留在口语里。

note.en: Words that look or sound close to tricky, and words that sit near it in meaning.
note.cn: 与 tricky 形近或音近的词，以及与它意思相近的词。

entries.definition: A clever act intended to deceive or amuse.
entries.definitionCN: 为欺骗或逗乐而使的花招；诀窍

entries.definition: To flow slowly in a thin stream.
entries.definitionCN: 细流；滴淌。只是拼写相近，词源与花招无关

entries.definition: Informal word for slightly itchy or ticklish.
entries.definitionCN: 发痒的（口语）。只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: Hard to do, understand, or deal with.
entries.definitionCN: 困难的；难做的。中性词，不强调暗藏圈套

entries.definition: Needing careful handling because things can easily go wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 微妙的；需要谨慎对待的。强调容易伤及各方，而非耍花招

entries.definition: Clever at deceiving people to get what one wants.
entries.definitionCN: 狡猾的；善于骗人的。强调聪明的欺骗，不带「难办」义

normalIntro.en: Five anchors built on the noun trick and its family.
normalIntro.cn: 围绕名词 trick 及其词族的五条记忆锚点。

normal.en: tricky = trick + y, so anything full of tricks is tricky.
normal.cn: tricky＝trick（花招）＋ -y，满是花招的东西自然「棘手」。

normal.en: a tricky question is a question that hides a trick.
normal.cn: a tricky question 就是暗藏花招、让人上当的题目。

normal.en: a tricky path makes you watch every step, like a path full of hidden tricks.
normal.cn: a tricky path 像布满暗算的路，每一步都得留神。

normal.en: a tricky customer plays tricks on you in business.
normal.cn: a tricky customer 做生意时专给人使绊子、耍滑头。

normal.en: trick (n.) is the base word; tricky, trickily and trickiness all grow from it.
normal.cn: trick 是词根，tricky、trickily、trickiness 都由它派生。

abstract.en: A wet stone on a mountain path: it looks ordinary until you step on it.
abstract.cn: 山路上一块湿滑的石头：看起来普通，踩上去才知道厉害。

abstract.en: A gift box that looks plain but springs a toy out when opened.
abstract.cn: 一个看似普通的礼盒，一打开就弹出一个玩具吓人一跳。

abstract.en: Walking an icy sidewalk: every step is calm, careful, and slightly dangerous.
abstract.cn: 走在结冰的人行道上：每一步都稳、小心，且暗藏危险。

examples.en: Parking in this narrow street is really tricky for beginners.
examples.cn: 在这条窄街停车对新手来说真的很棘手。

examples.en: The reporter asked a tricky question that the minister tried to dodge.
examples.cn: 记者提了一个刁钻的问题，部长试图回避。

examples.en: He can be a bit tricky in negotiations, so read every clause.
examples.cn: 他在谈判中有时不太老实，所以每个条款都要细读。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「垂克一」——垂着一根看不见的克线，走一步都被它「克」一下，路自然难走；此为谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 一般认为来自名词 trick（花招；欺骗），加形容词后缀 -y 构成「满是花招的」；trick 的更早来源为古法语 trique，与通俗拉丁语 triccare（耍花招）相关，深源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a hidden trick that catches you, and the senses move from hard situations to traps and then to deceitful people.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是「暗藏的圈套让你吃亏」：先指难办的局面，再指设了陷阱的题目，最后落到耍花招的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hidden trick waiting to catch you off guard
core.cn: 核心意象：一个藏在暗处、专门让你措手不及的花招

branches.en: Anything that behaves unexpectedly becomes hard to handle.
branches.cn: 凡是出人意料的东西都变得难对付。

branches.en: When the trick is set deliberately, the task turns into a trap.
branches.cn: 当花招是故意设下的，任务就变成了陷阱。

branches.en: Traps and surprises both force you to slow down and take care.
branches.cn: 陷阱与意外都逼你放慢脚步、加倍小心。

branches.en: A person who lives by tricks earns the label of deceitful.
branches.cn: 靠花招吃饭的人就被贴上「狡猾」的标签。

branches.en: Once you have been caught out, you stop trusting tricky people and tricky ground.
branches.cn: 吃过一次亏后，就不再轻信狡猾的人与敏感的话题。

intro.en: Tricky is a simple adjective built on trick; the items below show the suffixes and relatives around it.
intro.cn: tricky 是由 trick 加后缀构成的简单形容词，以下条目展示它周边的后缀与同族词。

latinIntro.en: The family is usually traced to Vulgar Latin triccare, though the link is not fully certain.
latinIntro.cn: 这一族词一般认为可追溯到通俗拉丁语 triccare，但证据并不完全确定。

items.example: trick + y gives tricky, full of tricks.
items.exampleCN: trick 加 -y 得到 tricky，即「满是花招的」。

items.meaningCN: 以某种方式（副词后缀，y 变 i）

items.example: trickiness, the quality of being tricky

items.meaning: a clever act meant to deceive or amuse
items.example: You cannot fool me with that old trick.
items.exampleCN: 你用那套老花招骗不了我。

items.meaning: the use of tricks to deceive
items.example: The deal was full of trickery.

items.meaning: a person who plays tricks on others
items.example: In old tales the trickster fox outwits everyone.
items.exampleCN: 在古老的故事里，狡猾的狐狸总是智胜所有人。

items.example: They tricked him into signing the paper.
items.exampleCN: 他们骗他签了那份文件。

definition_en: clear and fixed, not open to doubt; also easy to notice
core_image: 纸上一行字被框得方方正正，没有涂抹
scene: 她翻着日历，把下周的会面日期圈了两遍，却还留着一格空白。 We still have no definite date for the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 definite 指「明确的」（第 1 个义项：清楚而不含糊）；句意是我们还没有一个明确的会议日期。

senses.title: Clear and not vague
senses.definition: stated in a way that leaves no doubt about what is meant
senses.definitionCN: 说法清楚，让人对意思没有疑问
senses.example: We still have no definite date for the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 我们还没有一个明确的会议日期。
senses.why: A word with edges can be held; a vague one slips away.
senses.whyCN: 有边的话才拿得住，含糊的话会滑走。

senses.title: Certain in one's mind
senses.definition: sure that something is true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 确信某事为真或将会发生
senses.example: She was definite about her answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她对自己的回答很确定。
senses.why: Certainty is a room with the door closed.
senses.whyCN: 确定感就像一间关上了门的屋子。

senses.title: Easy to see or feel
senses.definition: large enough or strong enough to be noticed at once
senses.definitionCN: 大到或强到一眼就能察觉
senses.example: There is a definite change in the air.
senses.exampleCN: 空气里有一种明显的变化。
senses.why: What has edges also casts a shadow you cannot miss.
senses.whyCN: 有边的东西，投下的影子也让人没法忽略。

intro.en: Definite is the old past participle of define, so it carries the same picture of a line drawn around something.
intro.cn: definite 是 define 的古老过去分词，因此带着同样一幅「画线围住」的图景。

items.en: Definitus meant bounded, settled and brought to an end.
items.cn: definitus 意为有界的、定下的、已经结束的。

items.en: The word described a field with its corners marked.
items.cn: 这个词形容一块四角都标好的田。

items.en: Definit came into French as settled and certain.
items.cn: definit 进入法语时表示已定、确实。

items.en: English used it for answers, orders and grammar.
items.cn: 英语用它形容答复、命令和语法。

items.en: Grammar keeps the definite article for the one already known.
items.cn: 语法里仍用 definite article 指已经知道的那一个。

note.en: The look-alike group walks around the same fin stem, and the meaning group measures how sure a statement is.
note.cn: 形近组绕着同一个 fin 词干，近义组则衡量一句话有多确定。

entries.definition: to state the exact meaning of something
entries.definitionCN: 说明某事物的确切含义

entries.definition: final and not to be changed
entries.definitionCN: 最终的、不可更改的

entries.definition: having no end or limit
entries.definitionCN: 没有尽头或限度的

entries.definition: sure beyond doubt
entries.definitionCN: 毫无疑问地确信

entries.definition: easy to see or understand
entries.definitionCN: 容易看见或理解的

entries.definition: named exactly rather than in general
entries.definitionCN: 具体指明的，而非笼统的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a date circled twice and end with a change in the air nobody can miss.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从被圈了两遍的日期开始，落到空气里谁也躲不开的变化。

normal.en: A date is only a date when it is written down.
normal.cn: 日期只有写下来，才算一个日期。

normal.en: The definite article points at the cup you both already see.
normal.cn: 定冠词指的是你们都已经看见的那只杯子。

normal.en: A sure answer closes the door gently, not loudly.
normal.cn: 确定的回答是轻轻关门，而不是砰一声。

normal.en: When the air changes, you feel it before you can name it.
normal.cn: 空气一变，你先感觉到，后来才说得出。

normal.en: Definite and infinite are brothers, one with a fence and one without.
normal.cn: definite 与 infinite 是兄弟，一个带篱笆，一个没有。

abstract.en: Picture a square drawn in dust with a stick.
abstract.cn: 想象用一根树枝在灰土上画出一个方框。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing a page flat so nothing moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把纸压平，什么也不许动。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow on the wall that tells you someone is near.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一道影子，告诉你有人靠近。

examples.en: We still have no definite date for the meeting.
examples.cn: 我们还没有一个明确的会议日期。

examples.en: There is a definite change in the air.
examples.cn: 空气里有一种明显的变化。

examples.en: She was definite about her answer.
examples.cn: 她对自己的回答很确定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 definite 记成「定分你特」：de 开头，finite 是有限，界限分明，就是明确的。

root: 源自拉丁语 definitus，是 definire（划定界限）的过去分词，词根 finis 表示边界与终点。有边就有形，有形就不含糊，所以这个词从「划定的」引申出明确、确定与明显三层意思，语法上的定冠词也由此得名。

sensesIntro.en: From a bounded thing, to a closed mind, to a change too large to ignore.
sensesIntro.cn: 从有边有界的东西，到关上了门的心思，再到大到无法忽略的变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn neatly around a word.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈画得整整齐齐的线，围住一个词。

branches.en: The first sense is a statement with clear edges.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是边界清楚的一句话。

branches.en: The same clarity, inside a person, becomes certainty.
branches.cn: 同样的清楚放进人心里，就是确定。

branches.en: What is clearly bounded also stands out at once.
branches.cn: 界限清楚的东西，也一眼就能看出来。

branches.en: A clear answer and a sure mind are two sides of one line.
branches.cn: 清楚的答复与笃定的心思，是同一条线的两面。

branches.en: Both senses are about things that cannot be argued away.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指没法被说没的东西。

intro.en: Definite anchors a family of words about limits: define, definition, indefinite and definitive.
intro.cn: definite 撑起一族关于界限的词：define、definition、indefinite、definitive。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is finis, a boundary, with de- meaning completely.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 finis（边界），前缀 de- 表示彻底。

items.exampleCN: 这条定义适用于这种情况。
他们把任务界定得很清楚。

items.example: The definiteness of her tone surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 她语气的确定让我们吃惊。

items.example: The building stands empty for an indefinite time.
This is the definitive study of the river.
items.exampleCN: 这是关于这条河最权威的研究。

items.meaning: the word the, marking something known
items.meaningCN: 定冠词（指已知事物的 the）
items.example: Use the definite article before the noun.
items.exampleCN: 在这个名词前要用定冠词。

definition_en: a piece of cloth hung to cover a window, a stage, or anything that needs hiding
core_image: 米色布帘被拉开，午后的光从缝里涌进来
scene: 她拉开窗帘，让午后的光铺满地板。 She drew back the curtain and let the light in.
sceneCN: 这里 curtain 指「窗帘」（第 1 个义项：挂在窗上遮光挡视线的布）；句意是她拉开窗帘让光进来。

pos.zh: 给…装上窗帘；用帘子遮住

senses.title: Window cloth
senses.definition: a cloth hung over a window to block light or keep privacy
senses.definitionCN: 挂在窗上用于遮光或保护隐私的布
senses.example: She closed the curtains before the film.
senses.exampleCN: 电影开始前她拉上了窗帘。
senses.why: A window is a hole in the wall, and cloth decides how much of it stays open.
senses.whyCN: 窗户是墙上的一个洞，布决定这个洞开多大。

senses.title: Stage cloth
senses.definition: the large cloth that hides or reveals a stage
senses.definitionCN: 遮住或揭开舞台的大块布幕
senses.example: The curtain rose on a dark stage.
senses.exampleCN: 幕布在一片漆黑的舞台上拉开。
senses.why: Theatre needs a line between the world and the story.
senses.whyCN: 戏台需要一条线，把现实和故事隔开。

senses.title: A hanging screen
senses.definition: something that screens or hides, like a hanging cloth
senses.definitionCN: 像垂下的布一样遮挡或隐藏事物的东西
senses.example: A curtain of mist covered the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 一层雾幕盖住了山谷。
senses.why: Anything that falls between the eye and the thing can act as cloth.
senses.whyCN: 凡是落在眼睛与事物之间的，都能像布一样起作用。

intro.en: Curtain comes from Latin cortina, a curtain or cauldron, through Old French cortine.
intro.cn: curtain 源自拉丁语 cortina（帘幕、大锅），经古法语 cortine 进入英语。

items.en: Cortina named a curtain that screened a space.
items.cn: cortina 指用来隔开空间的帘幕。

items.en: The same word could also mean a round cauldron.
items.cn: 同一个词也能指一口圆锅。

items.en: Cortine kept the sense of a hanging screen of cloth.
items.cn: cortine 保留了垂挂布幕的意思。

items.en: Curtain first hung in churches and great halls.
items.cn: curtain 最初挂在教堂与大厅里。

items.en: The theatre gave it the sense of a stage curtain.
items.cn: 剧院赋予它舞台幕布的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cur- opening, and the meaning group names other things that screen a space.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cur- 开头，近义组列出其他遮挡空间的东西。

entries.definition: to cut short or reduce
entries.definitionCN: 缩短或削减

entries.definition: a small bow made by bending the knees
entries.definitionCN: 屈膝礼

entries.definition: to turn milk sour and thick
entries.definitionCN: 使牛奶变酸变稠

entries.definition: cloth hung in loose folds
entries.definitionCN: 松松垂下的布

entries.definition: a screen pulled down over a window
entries.definitionCN: 拉下来遮窗的帘子

entries.definition: a flat object that hides or divides
entries.definitionCN: 用来遮挡或隔开的平面物

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with light coming through a gap in cloth and end with mist that behaves like a curtain.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从布缝里透进来的光开始，落到像帘子一样起作用的雾。

normal.en: A curtain decides how much morning you deserve.
normal.cn: 窗帘决定你配得到多少早晨的光。

normal.en: On stage, the curtain is the line between two worlds.
normal.cn: 舞台上，幕布就是两个世界之间的那条线。

normal.en: Curtain call is the moment the cloth lets the actors be seen again.
normal.cn: 谢幕，就是布重新让演员被看见的那一刻。

normal.en: Mist can hang like a curtain with no rail at all.
normal.cn: 雾也能像帘子一样垂着，却不需要任何杆子。

normal.en: If cloth stands between you and the view, it is a curtain.
normal.cn: 如果一块布挡在你和风景之间，它就是帘子。

abstract.en: Picture a pale beam of light cut by a cloth edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一道苍白的光被布边切开。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy red cloth falling slowly on a stage.
abstract.cn: 想象一块厚重的红布在舞台上缓缓落下。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of rain moving across a field.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵雨墙从田野上推过去。

examples.en: She drew back the curtain and let the light in.
examples.cn: 她拉开窗帘，让光进来。

examples.en: The curtain rose on a dark stage.
examples.cn: 幕布在一片漆黑的舞台上拉开。

examples.en: A curtain of mist covered the valley.
examples.cn: 一层雾幕盖住了山谷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 curtain 记成「挡」：一块布挡在窗前是窗帘，挡在台前是幕布，挡在山前是雾幕。

root: 源自拉丁语 cortina（帘幕，也指圆锅），经古法语 cortine 进入英语；本义是挂在教堂与大厅里的隔断布，后来指窗帘与舞台幕布，再引申为一切遮挡物。

sensesIntro.en: From cloth across a window, to cloth across a stage, to anything that hangs between eye and world.
sensesIntro.cn: 从挡在窗前的布，到挡在台前的布，再到一切垂在眼睛与世界之间的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide cloth hung across an opening.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块宽大的布横挂在一个开口前。

branches.en: The first use is cloth over a window, ruling the light.
branches.cn: 最早的用法是窗上的布，管着光。

branches.en: The stage borrows the same cloth to hide its world.
branches.cn: 舞台借用同一块布，藏起自己的世界。

branches.en: Mist and rain can hang like cloth and hide a whole valley.
branches.cn: 雾和雨能像布一样垂着，藏起整片山谷。

branches.en: Window and stage both use cloth to time what is seen.
branches.cn: 窗户与舞台都用布来控制「什么时候被看见」。

branches.en: The stage curtain and the mist both mark a boundary.
branches.cn: 舞台幕布与雾幕，都在标记一条边界。

intro.en: Curtain is a Latin borrowing with a small English family, all built on hanging cloth.
intro.cn: curtain 是拉丁语借词，英语词族不大，全都围绕垂挂的布。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cortina, a curtain, is the source of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cortina（帘幕）是这一族词的来源。

items.example: The curtain moved in the wind.
The curtains were faded by sun.
items.exampleCN: 窗帘被太阳晒得褪了色。

items.example: A curtained window kept the room dark.
items.exampleCN: 挂着窗帘的窗让房间很暗。

items.example: They spent Sunday curtaining the hall.
items.exampleCN: 他们周日都在给大厅挂帘子。

items.meaning: a short play before the main one
items.exampleCN: 开场短剧演了二十分钟。

items.meaning: the moment actors return to bow
items.example: The crowd stood for the curtain call.

items.meaning: a cloth that keeps water in
items.example: Mould grew on the shower curtain.
They curtained off a corner of the room.
items.exampleCN: 他们把房间一角用帘子隔开。

definition_en: the feeling of being sorry for someone who is suffering
core_image: 一束白花放在门口，卡片上只写着一句节哀
scene: 她对他的失去深表同情。 She felt great sympathy for his loss.
sceneCN: 这里 sympathy 是「同情」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她对他的失去深表同情。

senses.title: Feeling sorry for another
senses.definition: the feeling of pity for someone in trouble
senses.definitionCN: 对困境中人的怜惜之情
senses.example: She felt great sympathy for his loss.
senses.exampleCN: 她对他的失去深表同情。
senses.why: The Greek source means shared feeling, so the noun names the emotion felt alongside another.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源头意为共同的感受，因此这个名词指与他人一同产生的情绪。

senses.title: The ability to feel for others
senses.definition: the capacity to understand another s suffering
senses.definitionCN: 理解他人痛苦的能力
senses.example: He has no sympathy for lazy excuses.
senses.exampleCN: 他对懒惰的借口毫无同情心。
senses.why: A single feeling became a lasting quality of character.
senses.whyCN: 一次的感受变成持久的品格。

senses.title: An expression of comfort
senses.definition: words or gifts offering comfort
senses.definitionCN: 表示安慰的话语或礼物
senses.example: They sent a letter of sympathy to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给那家人寄去慰问信。
senses.why: Feeling must be expressed, so the noun also names the message that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 感受需要表达，因此这个名词也指承载它的讯息。

senses.title: Agreement with a cause
senses.definition: support for an idea or group
senses.definitionCN: 对某个主张或群体的支持
senses.example: The workers acted in sympathy with the strike.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们声援这场罢工。
senses.why: Sharing feeling slides into sharing a purpose, which yields the sense of support.
senses.whyCN: 共感滑向共同的目标，于是产生支持之义。

intro.en: Sympathy comes from Greek sympatheia, feeling together.
intro.cn: sympathy 源自希腊语 sympatheia，意为共同感受。

items.en: Sympatheia named a shared condition or feeling.
items.cn: sympatheia 指共同的处境或感受。

items.en: Pathos meant what is felt or endured.
items.cn: pathos 意为所感或所受。

items.en: Late Latin sympathia kept the shared feeling sense.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 sympathia 保留共同感受之义。

items.en: Sympathy first described harmony between bodies.
items.cn: sympathy 最初描述物体之间的共鸣。

items.en: Sympathy settled on pity for another s trouble.
items.cn: sympathy 最终落定为对他人困苦的怜惜。

note.en: Sympathy is compared with look-alike words and with words for pity.
note.cn: 把 sympathy 与形近词以及表示怜悯的词作比较。

entries.definition: to share another s feeling
entries.definitionCN: 同情

entries.definition: showing care
entries.definitionCN: 同情的

entries.definition: a sign of illness
entries.definitionCN: 症状

entries.definition: deep pity for suffering
entries.definitionCN: 怜悯

normalIntro.en: The surface is the face a thing turns toward the world.
normalIntro.cn: surface 是一样东西朝向世界的脸。

normal.en: The surface of the table was smooth and clean.

normal.en: On the surface, the plan looks simple.

abstract.en: Every surface hides a depth it cannot show.
