definition_en: to take something into a larger whole so that it becomes one part of it
core_image: 两块面团被揉在一起，再也分不清哪块是新的
scene: 改稿时常常把别人的建议揉进自己的段落里。 The new plan incorporates ideas from every department.
sceneCN: 这里 incorporate 是「吸收合并」（第 2 个义项：把某物并进更大的整体）；句意是新计划吸收了各部门的想法。

pos.zh: 形容词：合并的；一体化的（多用于法律文本）

derivatives.zh: 由 incorporate 加 -ion 构成，义为「合并、法人化」
义为「已合并的、组成法人的」，公司名后常缩写为 Inc.
义为「公司的、团体的」，与本词同根

senses.title: To contain as an integrated part
senses.titleCN: 包含：作为整体中的一部分
senses.definition: to include something so that it forms part of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把某物纳入其中，使其成为整体的一部分
senses.example: The device incorporates a camera and a speaker.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设备里集成了摄像头和扬声器。
senses.why: The Latin corpus, body, supplies the image: something is given a body inside a larger body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 corpus「身体」提供了意象：某物被放进更大的身体里，获得了一个位置。

senses.title: To absorb ideas or material
senses.titleCN: 吸收：把想法或材料并进来
senses.definition: to take in suggestions, methods or substances and make them one's own
senses.definitionCN: 把建议、方法或材料吸收进来变成自己的
senses.example: The new plan incorporates ideas from every department.
senses.exampleCN: 新计划吸收了各部门的想法。
senses.why: Dough is the natural picture: once kneaded, the added piece cannot be taken back out.
senses.whyCN: 面团是最自然的画面：一旦揉进去，加进来的那块就取不出来了。

senses.title: To combine into one body
senses.titleCN: 合并：把两个单位并成一个
senses.definition: to unite two organizations or territories into a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 把两个组织或地区并成一个单位
senses.example: The two villages were incorporated into one town.
senses.exampleCN: 两个村庄合并成了一个镇。
senses.why: Law extends the body image to groups: several bodies may become one body.
senses.whyCN: 法律把身体意象扩展到团体：几个身体合成一个身体。

senses.title: To form a legal company
senses.definition: to establish a business as a legal corporation
senses.definitionCN: 把一家企业设立为法律上的法人公司
senses.example: They incorporated the business last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们去年春天把这家企业注册成了公司。
senses.why: A company receives a legal body of its own, which is exactly what the root promises.
senses.whyCN: 公司获得了自己的法律身体，这正是词根所许诺的意思。

intro.en: Incorporate comes from Late Latin incorporare, to give a body to, from in and corpus, body.
intro.cn: incorporate 来自晚期拉丁语 incorporare「赋予身体」，由 in 与 corpus「身体」构成。

items.en: Corpus meant a body, and also a body of writing or of people.
items.cn: corpus 意为「身体」，也指一批文字或一群人。

items.en: Incorporare meant to unite things into one body.
items.cn: incorporare 意为把多个事物联合成一个身体。

items.en: English used incorporate for mixing substances and ideas into a whole.
items.cn: 英语用 incorporate 表示把材料与想法混入整体。

items.en: Legal use produced the sense of forming a corporation.
items.cn: 法律用法产生了「组成法人公司」的含义。

items.en: Modern business writing uses it for features built into a product.
items.cn: 现代商务写作又用它表示产品里内置的功能。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the corpor- body root; the near-meaning group holds verbs of joining things into one.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「身体」的 corpor- 词根；近义组收表示「合为一体」的动词。

entries.definition: Relating to a large company.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「公司的、团体的」。

entries.definition: A company treated as one legal person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公司、法人团体」。

entries.definition: The act of uniting into one body.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「合并、法人化」。

entries.definition: To combine parts into a working whole.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「整合」，强调配合成完整系统。

entries.definition: To join two things so that they become one.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「合并」，多用于机构。

entries.definition: To take something in and make it part of oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吸收」，强调吞入并同化。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the body root, the kneaded dough and the company register.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「身体」词根、揉面的动作与公司注册。

normal.en: In plus corporate: put a body inside a body, and the smaller one loses its outline.
normal.cn: in 加 corporate：把一个身体放进另一个身体，小的那个就失去了轮廓。

normal.en: Corpus is body, so corporation is a group given one legal body.
normal.cn: corpus 是身体，所以 corporation 就是被赋予一个法律身体的团体。

normal.en: Kneading dough is the best demonstration: after folding, no one can find the seam.
normal.cn: 揉面团是最好的演示：折过之后没人找得到接缝。

normal.en: Inc. after a company name is this word cut short.
normal.cn: 公司名后的 Inc. 就是这个词的缩写。

normal.en: A good editor incorporates the reader's question without letting it show.
normal.cn: 好编辑会把读者的疑问吸收进去，却不让人看出来。

abstract.en: To incorporate is to make difference disappear without erasing its contribution.
abstract.cn: 吸收就是让差异消失，却不清除它带来的贡献。

abstract.en: Every culture grows by incorporating what it first called foreign.
abstract.cn: 每种文化都靠吸收当初称为「外来」的东西而成长。

abstract.en: A whole is strong when it can still name the parts it has taken in.
abstract.cn: 一个整体之所以强，是因为它仍叫得出自己吸收过哪些部分。

examples.en: The recipe incorporates a little honey for sweetness.
examples.cn: 这个食谱加了一点蜂蜜来增甜。

examples.en: Teachers incorporate games into the first lesson.
examples.cn: 老师们把游戏融入第一堂课。

examples.en: The firm was incorporated in nineteen ninety.
examples.cn: 这家公司于一九九零年注册成立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因科破瑞」——因为把学科破开重揉，就合并成了一门新学问。

root: 拉丁语 in（进入）+ corpus（身体）→ incorporare（赋予身体、合为一体）；同根词有 corporate、corporation、corpse、corps。

sensesIntro.en: Incorporate gives an incoming thing a body inside a larger body, so the word covers containing features, absorbing ideas, merging units and creating legal persons.
sensesIntro.cn: incorporate 让进来的东西在更大的身体里获得位置，因此涵盖内置功能、吸收想法、合并单位与成立法人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lumps of dough folded until the seam cannot be found.
core.cn: 核心意象：两块面团折叠到找不出接缝。

branches.en: PRODUCT LINE: a feature is built into the whole.
branches.cn: 产品线：某项功能被造进整体里。

branches.en: IDEA LINE: advice is kneaded into a plan.
branches.cn: 想法线：建议被揉进计划里。

branches.en: UNION LINE: two units are given one body.
branches.cn: 联合线：两个单位拥有同一个身体。

branches.en: LAW LINE: a business receives a legal body.
branches.cn: 法律线：企业获得法律意义上的身体。

branches.en: CRAFT LINE: the maker hides the joins but keeps the strength.
branches.cn: 手艺线：制作者把接缝藏起来，却保留强度。

intro.en: A Latin prefix for inside, a root meaning body, and a verb ending for making.
intro.cn: 一个表「在内」的拉丁前缀、一个意为「身体」的词根，以及表示「使之成为」的动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin corpus, body, with in and -are, gave incorporare, to make into one body.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 corpus「身体」结合 in 与 -are，构成 incorporare「使成一体」。

items.example: a body and a corpse share one root
items.exampleCN: 身体与尸体同出一个词根

definition_zh: 多样性、变化；种类、品种；（同一类的）若干不同事物；综艺节目
definition_en: a range of different kinds of the same thing, or one particular kind
core_image: 一个装满各色水果的篮子，每一样都不同，却都属于水果
scene: 菜市场的摊位上摆着十几种番茄，大小颜色各不相同。 The shop sells a wide variety of teas from the mountains.
sceneCN: 这里 variety 是「种类」（第 2 个义项：某一类中的一种）；句意为这家店出售山上产的各种茶叶。满篮各色果实互不相同的样子，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：多样性、变化；种类、品种；综艺节目

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「各种各样的」，是本词的形容词形式
形容词，义为「多样的、各不相同的」
形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」

senses.title: A range of kinds
senses.titleCN: 多样性：许多不同种类的集合
senses.definition: many different kinds of the same general thing
senses.definitionCN: 同一大类下许多不同的种类
senses.example: The market offers a wide variety of fruit in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天市场上水果种类很多。
senses.why: Latin varius means spotted or mixed; variety is the pattern of many kinds together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 varius 意为斑驳的、混杂的；variety 就是多种东西并置的图案。

senses.title: One kind among many
senses.titleCN: 种类：其中的某一个品种
senses.definition: a particular kind within a larger group, often a plant or product
senses.definitionCN: 较大类别中的某一具体种类，常指植物或产品
senses.example: The shop sells a wide variety of teas from the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售山上产的各种茶叶。
senses.why: The collective word narrows to a single item: this variety here, not the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 这个集合名词收窄为单个个体：是这一个品种，不是全部。

senses.title: Lack of sameness
senses.definition: the quality of not being all the same, valued as interest
senses.definitionCN: 不一模一样的性质，被视为有趣可贵
senses.example: A little variety in the menu keeps the children interested.
senses.exampleCN: 菜单上有点变化能让孩子们保持兴趣。
senses.why: Here the word judges rather than lists: sameness is dull, variety is good.
senses.whyCN: 这里的这个词在做评价而不是在列举：单调乏味，多样才好。

senses.title: A music hall show
senses.titleCN: 综艺：由多种节目拼成的演出
senses.definition: a show of separate acts such as singing, dance and comedy
senses.definitionCN: 由歌唱、舞蹈、滑稽戏等独立节目拼成的演出
senses.example: The theatre still puts on a variety show every winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这家剧院每到冬天仍上演综艺节目。
senses.why: A show of many acts is variety made visible: one stage, many kinds.
senses.whyCN: 多种节目同台就是可见的多样性：一个舞台，许多门类。

senses.title: A biological subspecies
senses.titleCN: 生物变种：人工培育或自然分化的品种
senses.definition: a group of plants or animals differing slightly from the species, such as a cultivated breed
senses.definitionCN: 与物种略有差异的动植物群体，如栽培品种
senses.example: This variety of apple ripens earlier than the others.
senses.exampleCN: 这个苹果品种比其他的成熟得早。
senses.why: Growers keep a stable set of traits and give it a name, and that named set is the variety.
senses.whyCN: 栽培者把一组稳定性状固定下来并给它命名，这个被命名的群体就是品种。

intro.en: Variety comes from Latin varietas through French, built on varius, meaning spotted or of many colours.
intro.cn: variety 经由法语来自拉丁语 varietas，词根 varius 意为斑驳的、多色的。

items.en: The adjective varius described skins, stones or animals marked with several colours.
items.cn: 形容词 varius 描述带多色斑纹的皮、石头或动物。

items.en: The noun varietas named diversity and difference, with the ending -tas for a state.
items.cn: 名词 varietas 指多样与差异，词尾 -tas 表示状态。

items.en: French carried variété into everyday use for the many kinds of a thing.
items.cn: 法语把 variété 带入日常使用，表示同一事物的许多种类。

items.en: English borrowed variety in the sixteenth century, first for diversity, then for a kind.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 variety，先表多样性，后表某一品种。

items.en: In the nineteenth century variety halls gave the word its show business sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪的杂耍剧院给了这个词演艺行业的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the vari- family; the near-meaning group holds words for range and for a single kind.
note.cn: 形近组是 vari- 家族；近义组收表示范围与单一品种的词。

entries.definition: Of several kinds; the adjective of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「各种各样的」，同词干的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb, to differ or change.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「变化、不同」。

entries.definition: A change or a changed version.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变化、变体」。

entries.definition: Something that changes; the technical cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」，技术性的近亲。

entries.definition: Difference among things, often used of people and species.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性」，常用于人群与物种。

entries.definition: The spread from one end to the other of a set.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「范围」，一套东西从头到尾的跨度。

entries.definition: A group of different things to choose from.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可供挑选的一组」，强调可挑选。

entries.definition: One kind of animal kept by people, closer to a single variety.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「品种」，更接近单个品种。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the basket-of-fruit core and phrases like a wide variety of.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「一篮果子」的意象与 a wide variety of 这类搭配。

normal.en: A variety of teas means many different teas, not one.
normal.cn: a variety of teas 指许多不同的茶，不是一种。

normal.en: Variety is the opposite of sameness in food, music and life.
normal.cn: variety 在食物、音乐和生活中都是「单调」的反面。

normal.en: A new variety of rice may ripen earlier than the old one.
normal.cn: 一个新稻种可能比旧的成熟得早。

normal.en: A variety show strings separate acts onto one stage.
normal.cn: variety show 把各种独立节目串在一个舞台上。

normal.en: Add variety to a routine and the routine stops feeling like a routine.
normal.cn: 给日常加点变化，日常就不再像日常。

abstract.en: The word holds both the whole and one piece of it: a variety of things, and the variety you picked.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时装下整体与一片：诸多种类，以及你选中的那一种。

abstract.en: Diversity is a pattern, not a list: it needs to be seen from above.
abstract.cn: 多样性是一种图案而非清单：它需要从上方看才成形。

abstract.en: Sameness repeats, variety remembers: a varied diet and a varied life both stay alive longer.
abstract.cn: 单调只是重复，多样带着记忆：多样的饮食与多样的生活都活得更久。

examples.en: The library offers a variety of books for young readers.
examples.cn: 这家图书馆为小读者提供各种图书。

examples.en: We stayed at home for a variety of reasons.
examples.cn: 我们待在家里，原因有好几种。

examples.en: This variety of tomato grows well in cool weather.
examples.cn: 这个番茄品种在凉爽天气里长得很好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我瑞爱提」——我瑞（锐）意爱提各种花样：多样性

root: 源自拉丁语名词 varietas（词根 varius「斑驳的、多样的」），经法语 variété 于十六世纪进入英语；同族词有 various、vary、variation、variable。

sensesIntro.en: Variety can mean many kinds together, one kind by itself, the pleasure of change, a stage show or a plant breed.
sensesIntro.cn: variety 可以指多种并存、单一品种、变化带来的趣味、综艺演出或植物品种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basket of fruit where every piece is a different kind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只篮子，里面每个果子都是不同种类。

branches.en: SET LINE: many kinds seen together.
branches.cn: 集合线：许多种类放在一起看。

branches.en: ITEM LINE: one particular breed or kind.
branches.cn: 个体线：某一个具体品种。

branches.en: PLEASURE LINE: change that keeps things interesting.
branches.cn: 趣味线：让人保持新鲜的变化。

branches.en: STAGE LINE: many acts in one show.
branches.cn: 舞台线：一场演出里许多节目。

branches.en: CONTRAST: variety is the whole basket, a kind is one fruit.
branches.cn: 对照线：variety 是整篮，a kind 是一个果子。

intro.en: Variety is a Latin state noun; its family supplies the adjective, verb and technical forms.
intro.cn: variety 是拉丁语状态名词，它的家族还提供形容词、动词与技术形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are varius, varietas and the adjective varius giving various.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁构件是 varius、varietas，而 various 直接来自 varius。

definition_en: relating to money, banking, or the management of funds
core_image: 银行大厅的屏幕上，一排排数字不停地跳动
scene: 这家公司正陷入财务困境。 The company is in financial trouble.
sceneCN: 这里 financial 是「财务的」（第 3 个义项）；句意：这家公司正陷入财务困境。

senses.title: Banking and investment
senses.definition: relating to banks, investments, and money markets
senses.definitionCN: 与银行、投资和货币市场有关的
senses.example: She works in the financial sector.
senses.exampleCN: 她在金融行业工作。
senses.why: This sense points to banks and investment.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项指向银行与投资领域。

senses.title: Public revenue
senses.definition: relating to the money of a government
senses.definitionCN: 与政府收支有关的
senses.example: The city faces a financial shortfall.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市面临财政短缺。
senses.why: Governments also manage money.
senses.whyCN: 政府同样要管理资金。

senses.title: Company accounts
senses.definition: relating to the money and accounts of a business
senses.definitionCN: 与企业的资金和账目有关的
senses.example: The company is in financial trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司正陷入财务困境。
senses.why: A business keeps its own accounts.
senses.whyCN: 企业有自己的账目要管。

intro.en: Financial goes back to Latin finis, an end, through French finance, a payment that settles a debt.
intro.cn: financial 上溯至拉丁语 finis（结束），经法语 finance（结清债务的付款）演变而来。

items.en: Finis meant an end or a boundary.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或边界。

items.en: Finare meant to settle a debt.
items.cn: finare 意为结清债务。

items.en: Finance named a payment or revenue.
items.cn: finance 指付款或收入。

items.en: Finance came to mean money management.
items.cn: finance 进而指资金管理。

items.en: The adjective financial described money matters.
items.cn: 形容词 financial 用来描述资金事务。

note.en: Financial is compared with similar-looking words and with words about money.
note.cn: 把 financial 与形近词以及表示金钱的词作比较。

entries.definition: the management of money
entries.definitionCN: 金融；财政

entries.definition: last in order
entries.definitionCN: 最后的

entries.definition: a person who deals in money
entries.definitionCN: 金融家

entries.definition: relating to money
entries.definitionCN: 货币的

entries.definition: relating to the economy
entries.definitionCN: 经济的

entries.definition: relating to public money
entries.definitionCN: 财政的

normalIntro.en: Financial is the adjective of finance, so it describes anything that involves money.
normalIntro.cn: financial 是 finance 的形容词，用来描述一切与金钱有关的事物。

normal.en: A financial crisis shakes the banks.
normal.cn: 金融危机让银行动荡。

normal.en: Financial aid helps students pay fees.
normal.cn: 经济援助帮学生支付学费。

normal.en: A financial adviser plans your money.
normal.cn: 理财顾问为你的钱做规划。

normal.en: The company reports financial results each year.
normal.cn: 公司每年公布财务业绩。

normal.en: Financial trouble means the money is short.
normal.cn: 财务困境意味着资金短缺。

abstract.en: Money is a promise that people agree to trust.
abstract.cn: 金钱是人们约定去信任的一种承诺。

abstract.en: A financial system turns trust into numbers.
abstract.cn: 金融体系把信任变成了数字。

abstract.en: Every account is a story of choices made.
abstract.cn: 每一本账目都是选择的故事。

examples.en: The company is in financial trouble.
examples.cn: 这家公司正陷入财务困境。

examples.en: She works in the financial sector.
examples.cn: 她在金融行业工作。

examples.en: They offered financial support to the family.
examples.cn: 他们向这家人提供了资金支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: financial 来自 finance（金融），加形容词后缀 -ial，表示「与资金有关的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 finis（结束），经法语 finance（结算、收入）演变为「财政、金融」。

sensesIntro.en: Financial describes matters of banking, public revenue, or company accounts.
sensesIntro.cn: financial 描述银行、政府收支或企业账目方面的事务。

core.en: Everything that belongs to money and its management.
core.cn: 一切属于金钱及其管理的事物。

branches.en: Belonging to banks and investment.
branches.cn: 属于银行与投资领域。

branches.en: Belonging to government money.
branches.cn: 属于政府资金。

branches.en: Belonging to a company's accounts.
branches.cn: 属于企业的账目。

branches.en: Both deal with large sums of money.
branches.cn: 两者都涉及大笔资金。

branches.en: Public and private books share the word.
branches.cn: 公共与私人账目共用一词。

intro.en: Financial is built from the noun finance plus the adjective suffix -ial.
intro.cn: financial 由名词 finance 加形容词后缀 -ial 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root finis, an end, also gave finish and final.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 finis（结束）也孕育了 finish 与 final。

items.exampleCN: 这个项目在财务上是稳健的。

items.example: The bridge was financed by the city.

items.exampleCN: 这位金融家资助了铁路。

latinEntries.example: Finis marks the end of a debt.
Finare meant to end a debt by paying.
latinEntries.exampleCN: finare 意为付款了结债务。

definition_en: a violent collision or its sound, or to hit something hard and break
core_image: 两辆车头撞在一起，玻璃碎成一地亮点
scene: 清晨的十字路口，两辆车头撞在一起，玻璃撒了一地。 The two cars crashed at the crossing.
sceneCN: 这里 crash 指「碰撞」（第 1 个义项：车辆猛烈相撞）；句意是两辆车在路口撞上了。

senses.title: Two things hitting hard
senses.definition: a violent collision between vehicles or objects
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或物体之间的猛烈相撞
senses.example: The crash blocked the whole road.
senses.exampleCN: 这场碰撞把整条路都堵住了。
senses.why: Two paths meet and both refuse to bend.
senses.whyCN: 两条路线相遇，两边都不肯让。

senses.title: An aircraft coming down
senses.definition: the falling and breaking of an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 飞行器坠落并损毁
senses.example: The plane crash was a terrible accident.
senses.exampleCN: 那场空难是一场可怕的意外。
senses.why: What flies must also obey the ground.
senses.whyCN: 会飞的东西，也终究要听地面的话。

senses.title: A market falling down
senses.definition: a sudden failure of a market or a system
senses.definitionCN: 市场或系统的突然失效
senses.example: The market crash ruined many families.
senses.exampleCN: 市场崩溃让许多家庭破了产。
senses.why: Numbers can fall as fast as metal can.
senses.whyCN: 数字下坠的速度，不比金属慢。

intro.en: Crash comes from Middle English crasschen, to make a loud clattering noise, a word built from its own sound.
intro.cn: crash 源自中古英语 crasschen（发出噼啪巨响），是照着声音造出来的词。

items.en: Crasschen meant to make a loud clattering noise.
items.cn: crasschen 意为发出响亮的碰撞声。

items.en: Crash named the sound of something breaking.
items.cn: crash 指东西碎裂时的响声。

items.en: It came to name a violent collision itself.
items.cn: 它转而来指猛烈碰撞这件事本身。

items.en: Crash widened to aircraft and to money markets.
items.cn: crash 又扩展到飞机与金融市场。

items.en: It now covers traffic, planes, computers and prices.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖交通、飞机、电脑与价格。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that begin with a hard cr-, and the meaning group names other words for violent impact.
note.cn: 形近组收集以硬辅音 cr- 开头的词，近义组列出其他表示猛烈撞击的说法。

entries.definition: to press something until it breaks
entries.definitionCN: 把东西压到碎裂

entries.definition: a sharp disagreement or fight
entries.definitionCN: 尖锐的冲突或争斗

entries.definition: a hard outer layer
entries.definitionCN: 坚硬的外层

entries.definition: the hitting together of two moving things
entries.definitionCN: 两个运动物体相撞

entries.definition: to break loudly into pieces
entries.definitionCN: 响亮地打成碎片

entries.definition: a badly damaged ship or vehicle
entries.definitionCN: 严重损毁的船或车

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two bumpers meeting, then move to a falling plane and to a falling market.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两个保险杠相碰开始，再到坠落的飞机，最后到崩落的市场。

normal.en: Crash sounds like what it means: a hard thing meeting a hard thing.
normal.cn: crash 读起来就像它的意思：硬东西撞上硬东西。

normal.en: Glass tells the story best, because it breaks all at once.
normal.cn: 玻璃最能说明问题，因为它是整片一起碎的。

normal.en: A crash course is a short road driven at full speed.
normal.cn: 速成课就是全速开完的一小段路。

normal.en: A plane crash ends in silence after the noise.
normal.cn: 空难总是在巨响之后归于寂静。

normal.en: Prices crash the way glass does: no warning, then nothing.
normal.cn: 价格崩落像玻璃：没有预告，然后什么都没有。

abstract.en: Picture two metal heads touching at speed.
abstract.cn: 想象两个金属车头高速相触。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a chart dropping straight down.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一条线笔直落下。

abstract.en: Picture a shower of small bright pieces on the road.
abstract.cn: 想象路面上撒开一片明亮的小碎片。

examples.en: The truck crashed into the fence.
examples.cn: 卡车撞上了篱笆。

examples.en: He survived a plane crash last winter.
examples.cn: 他去年冬天经历了一场空难并活了下来。

examples.en: The stock market crashed in a single day.
examples.cn: 股市在一天之内崩盘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crash 记成「咔嚓」加 sh：撞上去那一声碎响，就是 crash。

root: 源自中古英语 crasschen（发出噼啪巨响），是拟声词，本指物体碎裂的响声，后指猛烈碰撞，近代又扩展到飞机坠毁与市场崩溃。

sensesIntro.en: From two cars meeting to a plane coming down and a market losing its floor.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两车相撞，到飞机坠落，最后到市场失去支撑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hard fronts meeting with a burst of glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个坚硬的车头相撞，玻璃四溅。

branches.en: Two moving things reach the same point at once.
branches.cn: 两个运动的东西同时到达同一点。

branches.en: What flies can lose the air under it.
branches.cn: 会飞的东西也会失去身下的空气。

branches.en: A system built on numbers can fall like metal.
branches.cn: 建立在数字上的系统也能像金属一样跌落。

branches.en: Both end with broken parts on the ground.
branches.cn: 两者都以碎片落地收场。

branches.en: The same word covers a lost plane and a lost fortune.
branches.cn: 同一个词既说失事的飞机，也说失去的财富。

intro.en: Crash is an imitative base word that builds compounds with course, landing and proof.
intro.cn: crash 是拟声词根，可与 course、landing、proof 等组合成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English; Latin offers no source for this crash.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，拉丁语并不能给它提供来源。

items.example: The waves crashed on the rocks.
A crashing sound came from the hall.
A party crasher ate all the cake.
items.exampleCN: 一个闯入者吃光了蛋糕。

items.meaning: a short fast course of study
items.example: He took a crash course in Spanish.
items.exampleCN: 他上了一门西班牙语速成课。

items.meaning: a landing that damages the aircraft
items.example: The pilot made a crash landing.
